nodes.name: Adapted pressure (AP) ARZ model
nodes.statement: The AP ARZ model can be written as \begin{equation} \partial_t \mathbf{U} + \partial_x \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{U}) = {\bf 0}, \end{equation} where the conservative variable $\mathbf{U}$ and the flux function $\mathbf{F}$ are given by $\mathbf{U} = (\rho, y, z)^\top$, $\mathbf{F}(\mathbf{U}) = v \mathbf{U}$ with the density $\rho$ and the generalized momentum $y$.
nodes.statement_short: AP ARZ system $\partial_t U + \partial_x F(U)=0$ with $U=(\rho,y,z)$, $F=vU$.

nodes.name: AP ARZ conservation law (1.1)
nodes.statement: \partial_t \mathbf{U} + \partial_x \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{U}) = {\bf 0},
nodes.label: system

nodes.name: Driver behavior marker w and velocity v
nodes.statement: The ``driver behavior marker'' $w$ and velocity $v$ are respectively defined by $w = w(\mathbf{U}) := y/\rho$ and $v = v(\mathbf{U}) := w - p(\rho, z)$.

nodes.name: Pressure function p(rho,z)
nodes.statement: Here, the pressure $p(\rho, z)$ describes the response of drivers to changes in the density of the vehicle ahead. In this paper, we will consider the following pressure function: \begin{equation} p(\rho, z) = \left\{ \begin{aligned} & \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma} z^\kappa \rho^{\gamma-\kappa} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma} c^\kappa \rho^\gamma, \; && {\rm if} \; \gamma > 0, \\ & v_{\rm ref} \log{\rho}, \; && {\rm if} \; \gamma = 0 \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation} with a given reference velocity $v_{\rm ref}$ and parameter $\kappa \ge \gamma+1$.
nodes.statement_short: Pressure $p=\frac{v_{ref}}{\gamma} z^\kappa\rho^{\gamma-\kappa}$ for $\gamma>0$, $v_{ref}\log\rho$ for $\gamma=0$, with $\kappa\ge\gamma+1$.

nodes.name: Pressure function (1.2)
nodes.statement: p(\rho, z) = \left\{ \begin{aligned} & \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma} z^\kappa \rho^{\gamma-\kappa} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma} c^\kappa \rho^\gamma, \; && {\rm if} \; \gamma > 0, \\ & v_{\rm ref} \log{\rho}, \; && {\rm if} \; \gamma = 0 \end{aligned} \right.
nodes.label: P

nodes.name: Driver behavior label c
nodes.statement: Here, the variable $c = c(\mathbf{U}) := z/\rho > 0$ is used as a label to distinguish distinct ``driver behaviors'', and such a label is transported passively with traffic flow.

nodes.name: Eigenvalues of the AP ARZ Jacobian
nodes.statement: The eigenvalues of the Jacobian $\partial \mathbf{F}/\partial \mathbf{U}$ are $\lambda_1 = v-\rho p_\rho - z p_z$, $\lambda_2 = \lambda_3 = v$.

nodes.name: Original ARZ model
nodes.statement: If one sets $c \equiv 1$, then the AP ARZ model \eqref{system} degenerates into the original ARZ model \cite{aw2000resurrection}, and the pressure function \eqref{P} degenerates into the ones adopted in \cite{aw2000resurrection,BagneriniRascle2003,garavello2006traffic,herty2006optimization,haut2007second,chalons2007transport,FlynnKasimovNaveRosalesSeibold2009,betancourt2018random,buli2020discontinuous}.

nodes.name: Minimum and maximum principles for Riemann invariants of ARZ
nodes.statement: The Riemann invariants of \eqref{system} are $v$, $w$, and $c$. It holds that the solution to the system \eqref{system} satisfies minimum and maximum principles with respect to these Riemann invariants {\em globally} (see \cite{BagneriniRascle2003}), namely, \begin{equation} \mathbf{U}(x,t) \in \mathcal{I}^{\rm G},\qquad t > 0, \end{equation} where the global invariant domain $\mathcal{I}^{\rm G}$ is defined as \begin{equation} \mathcal{I}^{\rm G} := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : v \in [v^{\rm G}_{\min}, v^{\rm G}_{\max}], w \in [w^{\rm G}_{\min}, w^{\rm G}_{\max}], c \in [c^{\rm G}_{\min}, c^{\rm G}_{\max}] \right\} \end{equation} with the global upper and lower bounds of Riemann invariants defined as \begin{gather*} v^{\rm G}_{\min} := \min_x v(x,0), \quad w^{\rm G}_{\min} := \min_x w(x,0), \quad c^{\rm G}_{\min} := \min_x c(x,0), \\ v^{\rm G}_{\max} := \max_x v(x,0), \quad w^{\rm G}_{\max} := \max_x w(x,0), \quad c^{\rm G}_{\max} := \max_x c(x,0). \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Solutions of the AP ARZ system satisfy global min/max principles in the Riemann invariants $v,w,c$, i.e. stay in $\mathcal{I}^G$.
conclusions: the solution to the system \eqref{system} satisfies minimum and maximum principles with respect to these Riemann invariants {\em globally}

nodes.name: Global invariant domain inclusion (1.3)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{U}(x,t) \in \mathcal{I}^{\rm G},\qquad t > 0,
nodes.label: eq:328

nodes.name: Global invariant domain I^G (1.4)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{I}^{\rm G} := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : v \in [v^{\rm G}_{\min}, v^{\rm G}_{\max}], w \in [w^{\rm G}_{\min}, w^{\rm G}_{\max}], c \in [c^{\rm G}_{\min}, c^{\rm G}_{\max}] \right\}
nodes.label: eq:332

nodes.name: Local invariant domain principle
nodes.statement: The hyperbolic system \eqref{system} exhibits finite propagation speed, therefore, one may extend the global bound \eqref{eq:328} to a local version, $\mathbf{U}(x,t) \in \mathcal{I}^{\rm L}(x,t,t_0)$, $t > t_0 \geq 0$, where the local invariant domain $\mathcal{I}^{\rm L}(x,t,t_0)$ is defined as \begin{equation} \mathcal{I}^{\rm L}(x,t,t_0) := \left\{ \mathbf{U}= \left( \rho, y, z \right)^\top \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} v \in [v^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0), v^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0)] \\ w \in [w^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0), w^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0)] \\ c \in [c^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0), c^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0)] \end{array} \right\}, \end{equation} where the local bounds of Riemann invariants are defined as \begin{align*} v^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0) &:= \min_{\xi \in \mathcal{X}} v(\xi,t_0), & w^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0) &:= \min_{\xi \in \mathcal{X}} w(\xi,t_0), & c^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0) &:= \min_{\xi \in \mathcal{X}} c(\xi,t_0), \\ v^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0) &:= \max_{\xi \in \mathcal{X}} v(\xi,t_0), & w^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0) &:= \max_{\xi \in \mathcal{X}} w(\xi,t_0), & c^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0) &:= \max_{\xi \in \mathcal{X}} c(\xi,t_0). \end{align*} Here, the local domain of determination is defined as $\mathcal{X}:=[x-\alpha(t-t_0),x+\alpha(t-t_0)]$, and $\alpha$ denotes the maximum propagation speed.
nodes.statement_short: By finite propagation speed the solution stays in the local invariant domain $\mathcal{I}^L$ defined over the domain of determination.

nodes.name: Local invariant domain I^L (1.5)
nodes.statement: \mathcal{I}^{\rm L}(x,t,t_0) := \left\{ \mathbf{U}= \left( \rho, y, z \right)^\top \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} v \in [v^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0), v^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0)] \\ w \in [w^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0), w^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0)] \\ c \in [c^{\rm L}_{\min}(x,t,t_0), c^{\rm L}_{\max}(x,t,t_0)] \end{array} \right\},
nodes.label: eq:154

nodes.name: Strictly conservative BP scheme preserving v <= v_max
nodes.statement: While this random BP scheme is not strictly conservative, a natural question arises: Is it possible to design a strictly conservative BP method for the ARZ model that preserves \( v \le v_{\max} \)?

nodes.name: Impossibility of v maximum principle for conservative schemes (Betancourt et al. Prop. 4.1)
nodes.statement: By constructing a counter-example, Proposition 4.1 of \cite{betancourt2018random} provided a clear negative answer: no strictly conservative first-order scheme with a consistent two-point numerical flux can satisfy the \( v \) maximum principle.
conclusions: no strictly conservative first-order scheme with a consistent two-point numerical flux can satisfy the \( v \) maximum principle

nodes.name: v maximum principle conflict for AP ARZ
nodes.statement: Considering the AP ARZ model as a generalization of the ARZ model, this conflict between satisfying \( v \le v_{\max} \) and maintaining conservation/consistency also applies.
assumptions: Considering the AP ARZ model as a generalization of the ARZ model
conclusions: this conflict between satisfying \( v \le v_{\max} \) and maintaining conservation/consistency also applies

nodes.name: BP schemes for ARZ models with an alternative upper bound for v
nodes.statement: This leads to the new question: Is it possible to design BP schemes for the original and the AP ARZ models that satisfy the constraints in \eqref{eq:332} except \( v \le v_{\max} \), but adhere to another suitable upper bound for \( v \)?

nodes.name: Lax-Friedrichs (LF) splitting property
nodes.statement: When designing BP numerical schemes with the LF flux preserving invariant domain $\mathcal{I}$ for hyperbolic conservation laws, the following property \cite{zhang2010b,WuTang2015} is often desired and employed as the core of BP analysis: \begin{equation} \forall \, \mathbf{U} \in \mathcal{I} \; \Longrightarrow \; \mathcal{S}^\pm_{\tt LF}(\mathbf{U}) := \mathbf{U} \pm \frac{\mathbf{F}({\mathbf{U}})}{\alpha} \in \mathcal{I}, \end{equation} where $\alpha$ denotes an estimate of maximum propagation speed, and the above statement \eqref{eq:309} is typically called the LF splitting property \cite{WuTang2015} for $\mathcal{I}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{I}$ has the LF splitting property if $U\pm F(U)/\alpha\in\mathcal{I}$ for all $U\in\mathcal{I}$.

nodes.name: LF splitting property (1.6)
nodes.statement: \forall \, \mathbf{U} \in \mathcal{I} \; \Longrightarrow \; \mathcal{S}^\pm_{\tt LF}(\mathbf{U}) := \mathbf{U} \pm \frac{\mathbf{F}({\mathbf{U}})}{\alpha} \in \mathcal{I},
nodes.label: eq:309

nodes.name: LF splitting fails for the ARZ system
nodes.statement: Unfortunately, the statement \eqref{eq:309} does not generally hold for the system \eqref{system}--\eqref{P}, making the task of designing BP numerical schemes rather nontrivial.
conclusions: the statement \eqref{eq:309} does not generally hold for the system \eqref{system}--\eqref{P}

nodes.name: Generalized LF splitting property
nodes.statement: To overcome this difficulty, we investigate and prove the following generalized statement: \begin{equation} \forall \, \mathbf{U}_1, \mathbf{U}_2 \in \mathcal{I} \; \Longrightarrow \; \mathcal{S}_{\tt GLF}(\mathbf{U}_1,\mathbf{U}_2) := \frac12 \left[ \mathbf{U}_1 + \frac{\mathbf{F}({\mathbf{U}_1})}{\alpha} + \mathbf{U}_2 - \frac{\mathbf{F}({\mathbf{U}_2})}{\alpha} \right] \in \mathcal{I}, \end{equation} which is referred to as the generalized LF splitting property in the literature \cite{wu2018positivity}.
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{I}$ has the generalized LF splitting property if $\frac12[U_1+F(U_1)/\alpha+U_2-F(U_2)/\alpha]\in\mathcal{I}$ for $U_1,U_2\in\mathcal{I}$.

nodes.name: Generalized LF splitting property (1.7)
nodes.statement: \forall \, \mathbf{U}_1, \mathbf{U}_2 \in \mathcal{I} \; \Longrightarrow \; \mathcal{S}_{\tt GLF}(\mathbf{U}_1,\mathbf{U}_2) := \frac12 \left[ \mathbf{U}_1 + \frac{\mathbf{F}({\mathbf{U}_1})}{\alpha} + \mathbf{U}_2 - \frac{\mathbf{F}({\mathbf{U}_2})}{\alpha} \right] \in \mathcal{I},
nodes.label: eq:318

nodes.name: Invariant domains Omega_0, Omega_1, Omega_2, Omega
nodes.statement: In this paper, we consider the following invariant domains of the system \eqref{system}: \begin{align} \Omega_0 &:= \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \rho > 0, \; z > 0 \right\}, \nonumber \\ \Omega_1 &:= \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \rho > 0, \; w \in [w_{\min}, w_{\max}], \; c \in [c_{\min}, c_{\max}] \right\}, \nonumber \\ \Omega_2 &:= \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \rho > 0, \; z > 0, \; v \geq v_{\min} \right\}, \\ \Omega &:= \Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2 = \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z > 0, w \in \left[ w_{\min}, w_{\max} \right] \\ v \ge v_{\min}, c \in \left[ c_{\min}, c_{\max} \right] \end{array} \right\}. \end{align}
nodes.statement_short: Sets of states with positive density/z, bounded $w$, $c$, and $v\ge v_{min}$; $\Omega=\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2$.

nodes.name: Invariant domains Omega_0, Omega_1, Omega_2 (2.1)
nodes.statement: \Omega_0 &:= \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \rho > 0, \; z > 0 \right\}, \nonumber \\ \Omega_1 &:= \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \rho > 0, \; w \in [w_{\min}, w_{\max}], \; c \in [c_{\min}, c_{\max}] \right\}, \nonumber \\ \Omega_2 &:= \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \rho > 0, \; z > 0, \; v \geq v_{\min} \right\},
nodes.label: eq:O2

nodes.name: Invariant domain Omega (2.2)
nodes.statement: \Omega &:= \Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2 = \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z > 0, w \in \left[ w_{\min}, w_{\max} \right] \\ v \ge v_{\min}, c \in \left[ c_{\min}, c_{\max} \right] \end{array} \right\}.
nodes.label: eq:270

nodes.name: Alternative upper bound on v from w <= w_max
nodes.statement: Although the constraint $v \le v_{\max}$ is not directly addressed, the considered constraint $w \le w_{\max}$ actually implies another upper bound for $v$: \[ v = w-p(\rho,z) \le w_{\max} - p(\rho,z) \le \begin{dcases} w_{\max} & {\rm if }~ \gamma > 0, \\ w_{\max} - v_{\rm ref} \log (\min_x \rho) & {\rm if }~ \gamma = 0. \end{dcases} \] As one will see in the numerical experiments, this upper bound on $v$ can also help mitigate overshoots in $v$ in the numerical results.
nodes.statement_short: $w\le w_{max}$ yields $v\le w_{max}-p(\rho,z)$, an alternative upper bound on $v$.
nodes.label: rmk:435

nodes.name: Convexity of invariant domains
nodes.statement: The invariant domains $\Omega_0$, $\Omega_1$, $\Omega_2$, and $\Omega$ are all convex sets.
conclusions: The invariant domains $\Omega_0$, $\Omega_1$, $\Omega_2$, and $\Omega$ are all convex sets.
nodes.label: lem:466

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: {\sf Part I}: The set $\Omega_0$ is clearly convex. \noindent{\sf Part II}: For any two states $\mathbf{U}_0 = (\rho_0,y_0,z_0)^\top$ and $\mathbf{U}_1 = (\rho_1,y_1,z_1)^\top \in \Omega_1$, and any $\theta \in [0,1]$, let us denote $ (\rho_\theta, y_\theta, z_\theta)^\top = (1 - \theta) \mathbf{U}_0 + \theta \mathbf{U}_1$. In the following, we will prove that $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_1$. First, the positivity of $\rho_\theta$ can be obtained by $\rho_\theta = (1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1 \ge \min\{\rho_1,\rho_0\} > 0$. Since \begin{align*} w_\theta = \frac{y_\theta}{\rho_\theta} = \frac {(1 - \theta) y_0 + \theta y_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} & = \left( \frac{(1 - \theta) \rho_0}{(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) w_0 + \left( \frac {\theta \rho_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) w_1, \\ c_\theta = \frac{z_\theta}{\rho_\theta} = \frac {(1 - \theta) z_0 + \theta z_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} & = \left( \frac{(1 - \theta) \rho_0}{(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) c_0 + \left( \frac {\theta \rho_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) c_1, \end{align*} namely, $w_\theta$ (resp. $c_\theta$) is a convex combination of $w_0$ and $w_1$ (resp. $c_0$ and $c_1$), we have $w_\theta \in [w_{\min},w_{\max}]$ (resp. $c_\theta \in [c_{\min},c_{\max}]$). Thus, $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_1$ and $\Omega_1$ is convex. \\ {\sf Part III}: Now, let us assume $\mathbf{U}_0$ and $\mathbf{U}_1 \in \Omega_2$. The positivity of $z_\theta$ can be obtained by $z_\theta = (1 - \theta) z_0 + \theta z_1 \ge \min\{z_1,z_0\} > 0$. Additionally, we need to show $v_\theta \ge v_{\min}$. Consider a function of $\rho$ and $z$ defined as \begin{equation} \eta(\rho,z) := \rho (v_{\min} + p(\rho, z)) = y+\rho(v_{\min}-v) , \end{equation} such that for state $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,y,z)^\top$, the condition $v(\mathbf{U}) \ge v_{\min}$ is equivalent to $y \ge \eta(\rho,z)$. Since $y_\theta \ge \eta(\rho_\theta,z_\theta)$ for $\theta = 0$ and $1$, in order to prove $v_\theta \ge v_{\min}$, or equivalently, $y_\theta \ge \eta(\rho_\theta,z_\theta)$, we only need to show that the function $\eta(\rho,z)$ is convex for $(\rho,z) \in \mathbb{R}_+ \times \mathbb{R}_+$. To this end, we will show that its Hessian matrix $\mathbf{H}$ is positive semi-definite. In the case of $\gamma = 0$, the Hessian matrix is given by \( \mathbf{H} = {\rm diag}\{ v_{\rm ref}/\rho, 0 \}, \) which is clearly positive semi-definite. In the case of $\gamma > 0$, \[ \mathbf{H} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} \left(\begin{array}{cc} (\kappa-\gamma)(\kappa-\gamma-1) z^2 & -\kappa(\kappa-\gamma-1)z\rho \\ -\kappa(\kappa-\gamma-1)z\rho & \kappa (\kappa-1) \rho^2 \end{array}\right), \] and the determinants of its principle minors are given by \begin{gather*} \mathbf{H}_{11} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa+2}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} (\kappa-\gamma)(\kappa-\gamma-1) \ge 0, \quad \mathbf{H}_{22} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa+1} \kappa (\kappa-1) \ge 0, \\ |\mathbf{H}| = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa+2}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} \left[ (\gamma-\kappa)(\gamma-\kappa+1) \kappa(\kappa-1)-\kappa^2(\gamma-\kappa+1)^2 \right] \ge 0. \end{gather*} Thus, we conclude that $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_2$ and $\Omega_2$ is convex. \\ {\sf Part IV}: Since both $\Omega_1$ and $\Omega_2$ are convex, their intersection $\Omega$ is also convex.
nodes.statement_short: Convex combinations: $w_\theta$, $c_\theta$ are convex combinations; $v\ge v_{min}$ reduces to convexity of $\eta(\rho,z)$ via a PSD Hessian.

nodes.name: Auxiliary function eta (2.3)
nodes.statement: \eta(\rho,z) := \rho (v_{\min} + p(\rho, z)) = y+\rho(v_{\min}-v) ,
nodes.label: eq:406

nodes.name: Nonnegativity of the auxiliary function h
nodes.statement: Consider a function $h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z)$ for positive $\rho_*$, $z_*$, $\rho$, and $z$: \[ h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) := \rho \, \Big[ p(\rho, z) - p(\rho_*, z_*) \Big] + \rho_*\left[ \left(\rho_*-\rho\right) p_{\rho} (\rho_*, z_*) + \left(z_*-z\right) p_{z} (\rho_*, z_*) \right]. \] It holds that $h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \ge h(\rho,z;\rho,z) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: The function $h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z)$ built from the pressure is minimized at $(\rho_*,z_*)=(\rho,z)$, where it vanishes.
nodes.label: lem:791

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement: Note that \[ h_{z_*}(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) = \rho_*\left[ \left(\rho_*-\rho\right) p_{\rho z}(\rho_*, z_*) + (z_*-z) p_{zz}(\rho_*, z_*) + p_z(\rho_*, z_*) \right] -\rho p_z(\rho_*, z_*) \] We first consider the case of $\gamma > 0$. In this case, \[ h_{z_*}(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) = \frac{\kappa v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma} z_*^{\kappa-2} \rho_*^{\gamma-\kappa} \Big[ \gamma \rho_*z_* + (\kappa-\gamma-1) \rho z_* - (\kappa-1) \rho_* z \Big], \] which, due to $\kappa \ge \gamma+1$ and the positivities of $\rho_*$, $z_*$, $\rho$, and $z$, implies that \[ \begin{dcases} h_{z_*}(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) \ge 0 & {\rm if} ~ z_* \ge \frac{(\kappa-1) \rho_* z}{\gamma \rho_* + (\kappa-\gamma-1) \rho} =: z_\star, \\ h_{z_*}(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) < 0 & {\rm otherwise}. \end{dcases} \] Therefore, \begin{align*} h(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) \ge h\left(\rho_*, z_\star;\rho,z\right) = \rho p (\rho, z) - \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma} z \, \rho_*^{\gamma - \kappa + 1} z_\star^{\kappa - 1} =: \tilde{h}(\rho_*;\rho,z). \end{align*} Taking partial derivative of $\tilde{h}(\rho_*;\rho,z)$ with respect to $\rho_*$ gives \[ \tilde h_{\rho_*}(\rho_*;\rho,z) = v_{\rm ref} \frac{\kappa - \gamma - 1}{\kappa - 1} (\rho_* -\rho) \, \rho_* ^{\gamma -\kappa -1} z_\star^\kappa, \] which implies $\tilde h(\rho_*;\rho,z)$ is increasing with respect to $\rho_*$ if $\rho_* \ge \rho$, and decreasing if $\rho_* < \rho$. Therefore, $\tilde h(\rho_*;\rho,z) \ge \tilde h(\rho;\rho,z)$, and we finally have \[ h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \ge \tilde h(\rho_*;\rho,z) \ge \tilde h(\rho;\rho,z) = h(\rho,z;\rho,z) = 0. \] In the remaining case of $\gamma = 0$, $p(\rho,z) = v_{\rm ref} \log \rho$, and \[ h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) = v_{\rm ref} \left( \rho \log \rho - \rho \log \rho_* + \rho_* - \rho \right) =: \hat{h}(\rho_*;\rho). \] Taking derivative with respect to $\rho_*$ yields $\hat{h}_{\rho_*}(\rho_*;\rho)=v_{\rm ref}(\rho_*-\rho)/\rho_*$, indicating $\hat{h}(\rho_*;\rho)$ is increasing with respect to $\rho_*$ if $\rho_* \ge \rho$, and decreasing if $\rho_* < \rho$. Therefore, in the case of $\gamma = 0$, we conclude the proof by \[ h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \ge \hat{h}(\rho_*;\rho) \ge \hat{h}(\rho;\rho) = h(\rho,z;\rho,z) = 0. \]
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on $\gamma$: minimize $h$ over $z_*$ via the sign of $h_{z_*}$, then over $\rho_*$ via monotonicity of the reduced function.

nodes.name: LF splitting property for Omega_1
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,y,z)^\top \in \Omega_1$, then the LF splitting form $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm := \mathcal{S}^\pm_{\tt LF}(\mathbf{U}) = \mathbf{U} \pm \alpha^{-1} \mathbf{F} (\mathbf{U}) \in \Omega_1$ provided that $\alpha > v(\mathbf{U}) > 0$.
nodes.label: L1

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.3
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm = (\hat{\rho}_\pm,\hat{y}_\pm,\hat{z}_\pm)^\top$, $\hat{v}_\pm = v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm)$, $\hat{w}_\pm = w(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm)$, and $\hat{c}_\pm = c(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm)$. Because $\alpha > v(\mathbf{U}) > 0$, we have $\hat{\rho}_\pm = \left( 1 \pm v(\mathbf{U})/\alpha \right) \rho > 0$, and \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \hat{w}_\pm - w_{\min} & = {(\hat{y}_\pm - \hat{\rho}_\pm \, w_{\min})}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} = \left( 1 \pm {v(\mathbf{U})}/{\alpha} \right) \left( {\rho}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm}\right) (w - w_{\min}) \geq 0, \\ w_{\max} - \hat{w}_\pm & = {(\hat{\rho}_\pm \, w_{\max} - \hat{y}_\pm)}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} = \left( 1 \pm {v(\mathbf{U})}/{\alpha} \right) \left( {\rho}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} \right) (w_{\max} - w) \geq 0, \\ \hat{c}_\pm - c_{\min} & = {(\hat{z}_\pm - \hat{\rho}_\pm \, c_{\min})}{\hat{\rho}_\pm} = \left( 1 \pm {v(\mathbf{U})}/{\alpha} \right) \left( {\rho}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} \right) (c - c_{\min}) \geq 0, \\ c_{\max} - \hat{c}_\pm & = {(\hat{\rho}_\pm \, c_{\max} - \hat{z}_\pm)}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} = \left( 1 \pm {v(\mathbf{U})}/{\alpha} \right) \left( {\rho}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} \right) (c_{\max} - c) \geq 0. \end{aligned} \end{equation*} In summary, $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm \in \Omega_1$. The proof is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation: $\hat\rho_\pm>0$ and the bound gaps of $\hat w_\pm$, $\hat c_\pm$ are positive multiples of those of $w$, $c$.

nodes.name: GQL representation of Omega_2
nodes.statement: The set $\Omega_2$ is equivalent to \begin{equation*} \Omega_2^* := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \rho > 0, \; z > 0, \; \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* \geq 0 \quad \forall \; \rho_* > 0, \; z_* > 0 \right\}, \end{equation*} where $\mathbf{n}_* := \mathbf{n}(\rho_*,z_*)$, $s_* := s(\rho_*,z_*)$, \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{n}(\rho,z) &:= - \left(v_{\min} + p (\rho, z) + \rho p_\rho(\rho, z), -1, \rho p_{z} (\rho, z) \right)^\top, \\ s(\rho,z) &:= \rho^2 p_\rho (\rho, z) + \rho z p_z (\rho, z). \end{aligned} \end{equation*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.4
nodes.statement: On one hand, if $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,y,z)^\top \in \Omega_2$, then, $\rho > 0$, $z > 0$. Notice that, for any $\rho_* > 0$ and $z_* > 0$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* &= y - \rho \big( v_{\min} + p(\rho,z)\big) + h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \\ &\stackrel{\rm \Cref{lem:791}}{\ge} y - \rho \big( v_{\min} + p(\rho,z)\big) = \rho \big( v(\mathbf{U}) - v_{\min}\big) \ge 0 , \end{aligned} \end{equation} which implies that $\mathbf{U} \in \Omega_2^*$. On the other hand, if $\mathbf{U} \in \Omega_2^*$, then $\rho > 0$, $z > 0$. Notice that $\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* \ge 0$ for any $\rho_* > 0$ and $z_* > 0$. Taking $\rho_* = \rho$ and $z_* = z$ implies \[ \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}(\rho,z) + s(\rho,z) = y - \rho \big( v_{\min} + p(\rho,z)\big) = \rho \big( v(\mathbf{U}) - v_{\min}\big) \ge 0. \] Therefore, it holds that $\mathbf{U} \in \Omega_2$. The proof is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Two inclusions: Lemma 2.2 gives $U\cdot n_*+s_*\ge\rho(v-v_{min})\ge0$; conversely take $\rho_*=\rho$, $z_*=z$.

\mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{y}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{y}}$} } y,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 \geq 0 \end{equation} holds for any $\rho_* > 0, z_* > 0$, under the condition \begin{equation} \alpha \geq \alpha_{\max}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}},\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) := \max \Big\{ \alpha_{\rm std} , |v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})|+\overline{s}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}},\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})/\,\check{\rho}\, \Big\}. \end{equation} Here, $\alpha_{\rm std} := \max \{ \overline\alpha(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}), \overline\alpha(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\}$, $\overline \alpha(\mathbf{U})$ $:= v + |\rho p_{\rho}+z p_z|$ is an estimate of the maximum propagation speed, \begin{equation} \overline{s}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}},\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) := \max_ {\substack{ \rho \in [\underline{\rho},\overline{\rho}] \\ z \in [\underline{z},\overline{z}] } } s(\rho,z) = \begin{dcases} v_{\rm ref} \overline{z}^{\,\kappa}\, \underline{\rho}^{\gamma-\kappa} & {\rm if}~ \gamma > 0, \\ v_{\rm ref} \, \overline\rho & {\rm if}~ \gamma = 0, \end{dcases} \end{equation} \begin{align*} + \frac{\hat{\rho}\;\hat{v} - \check{\rho}\;\check{v}}{2 \alpha_{\rm std}}, \\ \underline{z} &:= \min \left\{z_1,{z}_2\right\},& \; \overline{z} &:= \max \left\{{z}_1,{z}_2\right\},& \; {z}_1 &:= \frac{\hat{z}+\check{z} }{2},& \; {z}_2 &:= z_1 + \frac{\hat{z}\;\hat{v} - \check{z}\;\check{v}}{2 \alpha_{\rm std}}. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.5
nodes.statement: For any $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,y,z)^\top \in \Omega_2^*$, we denote $v = v(\mathbf{U}) \ge v_{\min}$, then \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} & ~~~ \pm \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{U}) \cdot \mathbf{n}_* \pm v_{\min} s_* \\ & = \pm v \, (\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) \pm (v_{\min}-v) s_* \le |v|\,(\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) +\frac{s_*}{\rho}\Big[ \rho (v-v_{\min}) \Big] \\ & \stackrel{\eqref{eq:632}}{\le} \, |v|\,(\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) + \frac{s_*}{\rho}(\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) = \left( |v|+\frac{s_*}{\rho} \right) (\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) , \end{aligned} \end{equation} where the last inequality is due to \begin{equation} \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* = \rho (v-v_{\min}) + h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \stackrel{\rm \Cref{lem:791}}{\ge} \rho (v-v_{\min}). \end{equation} Let us denote $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{v}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{v}}$} } v = v(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U})$, $\widehat{\mathbf{F}} = \mathbf{F}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})$, and $\widecheck{\mathbf{F}} = \mathbf{F}(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})$, then it implies \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} 2\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + 2s_* & = \left[~ \widehat{\mathbf{U}} + \alpha^{-1} \widehat{\mathbf{F}} + \widecheck{\mathbf{U}} - \alpha^{-1} \widecheck{\mathbf{F}} ~\right] \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + 2 s_* \\ & = \widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + \widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + \alpha^{-1} \left( \widehat{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* - \widecheck{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + v_{\min} s_* - v_{\min} s_* \right) + 2 s_* \\ & = \widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + \widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + 2s_* - \alpha^{-1} \left( \widecheck{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + v_{\min} s_* \right) - \alpha^{-1} \left(-\widehat{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* - v_{\min} s_* \right) \\ & \stackrel{\eqref{eq:669}}{\ge} \left(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_*+s_*\right) - \alpha^{-1} \left( \left|v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\right|+\frac{s_*}{\hat{\rho}}\right) (\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) \\ & \hspace{5mm} + \left(\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_*+s_*\right) - \alpha^{-1} \left( \left|v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\right|+\frac{s_*}{\hat{\rho}}\right) (\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) \\ & = \alpha^{-1} \left(\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_*+s_*\right) \left(\alpha-\left|v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\right|-\frac{s_*}{\hat{\rho}}\right) + \alpha^{-1} \left(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_*+s_*\right) \left(\alpha-\left|v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\right|-\frac{s_*}{\check{\rho}}\right). \end{aligned} \end{equation} Additionally, for any $\rho_* > 0$ and $z_* > 0$, \begin{align*} & 2 \Big( \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* \Big) = 2 \Big[ \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho (\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{v}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{v}}$} } v-v_{\min}) + h(\rho_*,z_*;\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z) \Big] \\ \stackrel{\rm \Cref{lem:791}}{\ge} & 2 \Big[ \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho (\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{v}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{v}}$} } v-v_{\min}) + h(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 z;\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho, \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z) \Big] = 2 \left[\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z) + s (\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z) \right] \\ \stackrel{\eqref{eq:726}}{\ge} \hspace{3.5mm} & \alpha^{-1}\left(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}\cdot\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathbf{n}+\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s\right) \left(\alpha-\left|v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\right|-\frac{\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s}{\hat{\rho}}\right) + \alpha^{-1}\left(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}\cdot\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathbf{n}+\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s\right) \left(\alpha-\left|v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\right|-\frac{\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s}{\check{\rho}}\right), \end{align*} where $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathbf{n} := \mathbf{n}(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z)$ and $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s := s(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z)$. Thus, to prove \eqref{eq:656}, we only need to show that $ \alpha \ge \left|v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\right|+{\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s}/{\hat{\rho}} $ and $ \alpha \ge \left|v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\right|+{\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s}/{\check{\rho}} $ . Based on the inequality \eqref{eq:674}, we only need to show $\overline{s}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}},\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \ge \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s$. To this end, according to $\overline{s}$ in \eqref{eq:686}, it is sufficient to prove that \begin{equation} \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho \in \big[\,\underline{\rho},\overline{\rho}\,\big], \qquad \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z \in \big[\,\underline{z},\overline{z}\,\big]. \end{equation} Notice that \begin{align*} \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho = \frac{\hat{\rho}}{2}\left(1+\frac{\hat{v}}{\alpha}\right) +& \frac{\check{\rho}}{2}\left(1-\frac{\check{v}}{\alpha}\right) = \frac{\hat{\rho}+\check{\rho}}{2} + \alpha^{-1} \left( \frac{\hat{\rho}\hat{v}-\check{\rho}\check{v}}{2} \right), \\ \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z = \frac{\hat{z}}{2}\left(1+\frac{\hat{v}}{\alpha}\right) +& \frac{\check{z}}{2}\left(1-\frac{\check{v}}{\alpha}\right) = \frac{\hat{z}+\check{z}}{2} + \alpha^{-1} \left( \frac{\hat{z}\hat{v}-\check{z}\check{v}}{2} \right) \end{align*} are both linear functions with respect to $\alpha^{-1}$. Based on the condition \eqref{eq:674}, $\alpha^{-1} \in \big(\,0,\alpha_{\rm std}^{-1}\,\big]$, which implies the value of $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho$ (resp. $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z$) is between $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ (resp. $z_1$ and $z_2$). Thus, \eqref{eq:1010} is true. The proof is completed.

nodes.name: Range of GLF density and z (2.11)
nodes.statement: \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho \in \big[\,\underline{\rho},\overline{\rho}\,\big], \qquad \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z \in \big[\,\underline{z},\overline{z}\,\big].
