nodes.name: Generalized LF splitting property for Omega
nodes.statement: If $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}=(\hat{\rho},\hat{y},\hat{z})^\top \in \Omega$ and $\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}=(\check{\rho},\check{y},\check{z})^\top \in \Omega$, then $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} = (\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{y}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{y}}$} } y,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z)^\top$ $:= \mathcal{S}_{\tt GLF}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}},\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\in \Omega$, under the condition $\alpha > \alpha_{\max}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}},\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})$.
nodes.statement_short: The GLF combination of two states in $\Omega$ remains in $\Omega$ when $\alpha>\alpha_{max}$.
nodes.label: thm:1471

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.6
nodes.statement: On one hand, Since $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}$, $\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \in \Omega \subseteq \Omega_2 = \Omega_2^*$, \Cref{L2} implies that $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \in \Omega_2^* = \Omega_2$. On the other hand, since $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}$, $\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \in \Omega \subseteq \Omega_1$, and $\alpha > \alpha_{\max}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}, \widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \ge \max\{ v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}), v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \}$, \Cref{L1} implies $\mathcal{S}^+_{\tt LF}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})$, $\mathcal{S}^-_{\tt LF}(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \in \Omega_1$. The convexity of $\Omega_1$ (\Cref{lem:466}) implies $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} = \frac12\mathcal{S}^+_{\tt LF}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})+\frac12\mathcal{S}^-_{\tt LF}(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \in \Omega_1$. Therefore, it holds that $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \in \Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2 = \Omega$, and the proof is completed.
nodes.statement_short: Combine Lemma 2.5 (membership in $\Omega_2$) with Lemma 2.3 and convexity of $\Omega_1$ (Lemma 2.1).

nodes.name: Uniform spatial mesh
nodes.statement: Assume that the spatial domain $\mathcal{D}$ is divided into $N_x$ uniform cells $\big\{ \, I_j := [x_{j - \frac{1}{2}}, x_{j + \frac{1}{2}}] \, \big\}_{j=1}^{N_x}$ with size $\Delta x$ and center $x_j = \frac{1}{2} (x_{j - \frac{1}{2}} + x_{j + \frac{1}{2}})$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: Time mesh
nodes.statement: The time interval is divided into a mesh $\big\{ t_0 = 0, \; t_{n + 1} =$ $ t_n + \Delta t_n, \; n \geq 0\big\}$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: Cell average
nodes.statement: Let $\overline{\mathbf{U}}_j^n$ denote the cell-averaged approximation of the exact solution $\mathbf{U}(x, t)$ over $I_j$ at time $t = t_n$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: DG finite element space V_h^k
nodes.statement: Let $\mathbf{U}_h (x,\cdot)$ be a piecewise polynomial vector function of degree $k$, namely, \begin{equation*} \mathbf{U}_h (x,\cdot) \in \mathbb{V}_h^k := \left\{~ \mathbf{U}(x) = (\rho_h(x), y_h(x), z_h(x))^\top: \rho_h \vert_{I_j}, y_h \vert_{I_j}, z_h \vert_{I_j} \in \mathbb{P}^k (I_j) \; \forall j ~\right\}, \end{equation*} where $\mathbb{P}^k (I_j)$ denotes the space of polynomials of degree up to $k$ on $I_j$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: DG spatial discretization (weak form)
nodes.statement: Multiplying the system \eqref{system} with a test function $\phi(x) \in \mathbb{P}^k (I_j)$, and integrating by parts over $I_j$ yields \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \frac{\rm d}{{\rm d} t} \int_{I_j} \mathbf{U}_h(x,t) \, \phi(x) \, {\rm d} x = & \int_{I_j} \mathbf{F} (\mathbf{U}_h) \frac{{\rm d} \phi}{{\rm d} x} {\rm d} x + \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{U}_h (x_{j - \frac{1}{2}},t ) \right) \phi ( x_{j - \frac{1}{2}} ) \\ & - \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{U}_h (x_{j + \frac{1}{2}},t ) \right) \phi ( x_{j + \frac{1}{2}} ), \end{aligned} \end{equation} where we have replaced the exact solution $\mathbf{U}(x,t)$ with the approximation solution $\mathbf{U}_h(x,t)$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: DG weak formulation (3.1)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \frac{\rm d}{{\rm d} t} \int_{I_j} \mathbf{U}_h(x,t) \, \phi(x) \, {\rm d} x = & \int_{I_j} \mathbf{F} (\mathbf{U}_h) \frac{{\rm d} \phi}{{\rm d} x} {\rm d} x + \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{U}_h (x_{j - \frac{1}{2}},t ) \right) \phi ( x_{j - \frac{1}{2}} ) \\ & - \mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{U}_h (x_{j + \frac{1}{2}},t ) \right) \phi ( x_{j + \frac{1}{2}} ), \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.label: DG

nodes.name: Modal expansion of the DG solution
nodes.statement: Let $\big\{ \phi_j^{[\ell]}(x) \big\}_{\ell = 0}^k$ denote a local orthogonal basis of the polynomial space $\mathbb{P}^k (I_j)$, then one can decompose the DG approximate solution $\mathbf{U}_h(x,t)$ as \begin{equation} \mathbf{U}_h (x,t) = \sum_{j} \mathbbm{1}_{I_j}(x) \, \mathbf{U}_j (x, t), \quad \mathbf{U}_j (x,t) := \sum_{\ell = 0}^k \mathbf{U}_j^{[\ell]} (t) \phi_j^{[\ell]} (x) . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: Modal expansion (3.2)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{U}_h (x,t) = \sum_{j} \mathbbm{1}_{I_j}(x) \, \mathbf{U}_j (x, t), \quad \mathbf{U}_j (x,t) := \sum_{\ell = 0}^k \mathbf{U}_j^{[\ell]} (t) \phi_j^{[\ell]} (x) .
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.label: basis

nodes.name: DG scheme with LF numerical flux
nodes.statement: Substituting \eqref{basis} into \eqref{DG}, replacing $\phi(x)$ with basis function $\phi_j^{[\ell]} (x)$, and approximating $\mathbf{F} \left(\mathbf{U}_h (t, x_{j \pm \frac{1}{2}} ) \right)$ with numerical fluxes $\widehat{\mathbf{F}} \left( \mathbf{U}^-_{j \pm \frac{1}{2}}, \mathbf{U}^+_{j \pm \frac{1}{2}} \right) $ results in \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \frac{\rm d}{{\rm d} t} \mathbf{U}_j^{[\ell]} (t) = \frac{2 \ell + 1}{\Delta x} & \bigg[ \int_{I_j} \mathbf{F} (\mathbf{U}_h) \frac{{\rm d} \phi_j^{[\ell]} (x)}{{\rm d} x} {\rm d} x + \widehat{\mathbf{F}} \left( \mathbf{U}^-_{j - \frac{1}{2}}, \mathbf{U}^+_{j - \frac{1}{2}} \right) \phi_j^{[\ell]} (x_{j - \frac{1}{2}}) \\ & - \widehat{\mathbf{F}} \left( \mathbf{U}^-_{j + \frac{1}{2}}, \mathbf{U}^+_{j + \frac{1}{2}} \right) \phi_j^{[\ell]} (x_{j + \frac{1}{2}}) \bigg], \end{aligned} \end{equation*} where $\widehat{\mathbf{F}} \left( \cdot, \cdot \right) $ is a two-point numerical flux, for example, the LF numerical flux: \begin{equation*} \widehat{\mathbf{F}} ( \mathbf{U}^-, \mathbf{U}^+ ) = \frac12 \left[ \mathbf{F} ( \mathbf{U}^- ) + \mathbf{F} ( \mathbf{U}^+ ) - \alpha ( \mathbf{U}^+ - \mathbf{U}^- ) \right]. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: Modal DG ODEs with a two-point numerical flux, e.g. LF flux $\frac12[F(U^-)+F(U^+)-\alpha(U^+-U^-)]$.

nodes.name: Modal DG scheme
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \frac{\rm d}{{\rm d} t} \mathbf{U}_j^{[\ell]} (t) = \frac{2 \ell + 1}{\Delta x} & \bigg[ \int_{I_j} \mathbf{F} (\mathbf{U}_h) \frac{{\rm d} \phi_j^{[\ell]} (x)}{{\rm d} x} {\rm d} x + \widehat{\mathbf{F}} \left( \mathbf{U}^-_{j - \frac{1}{2}}, \mathbf{U}^+_{j - \frac{1}{2}} \right) \phi_j^{[\ell]} (x_{j - \frac{1}{2}}) \\ & - \widehat{\mathbf{F}} \left( \mathbf{U}^-_{j + \frac{1}{2}}, \mathbf{U}^+_{j + \frac{1}{2}} \right) \phi_j^{[\ell]} (x_{j + \frac{1}{2}}) \bigg], \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.label: DGmethod

nodes.name: LF numerical flux
nodes.statement: \widehat{\mathbf{F}} ( \mathbf{U}^-, \mathbf{U}^+ ) = \frac12 \left[ \mathbf{F} ( \mathbf{U}^- ) + \mathbf{F} ( \mathbf{U}^+ ) - \alpha ( \mathbf{U}^+ - \mathbf{U}^- ) \right].
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.label: LF

nodes.name: Interface limits U^pm_{j+1/2}
nodes.statement: The states $\mathbf{U}^-_{j + \frac{1}{2}}$ and $\mathbf{U}^+_{j + \frac{1}{2}}$ respectively denote the left- and right-limits of $\mathbf{U}_h$ at $x_{j+\frac12}$: $\mathbf{U}^{+}_{j + \frac{1}{2}} := \mathbf{U}_{j+1}(x_{j+\frac12})$, $\mathbf{U}^{-}_{j + \frac{1}{2}}:=\mathbf{U}_{j}(x_{j+\frac12})$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: Third-order SSP Runge-Kutta time discretization
nodes.statement: We may rewrite the semidiscrete scheme \eqref{DG} in an ODE form $\frac{\rm d}{{\rm d} t} \mathbf{U}_h = \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}_h)$, and discretize it in time with, for example, the classic explicit third-order strong-stability-preserving (SSP) Runge--Kutta (RK) method: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} = \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}_h^{n} \right), \\ &\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} = \frac{3}{4} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{1}{4} \left[ \mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} \right) \right], \\ &\mathbf{U}_h^{n + 1} = \frac{1}{3} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{2}{3} \left[ \mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} \right) \right]. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: SSP-RK3 (3.3)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} = \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}_h^{n} \right), \\ &\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} = \frac{3}{4} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{1}{4} \left[ \mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} \right) \right], \\ &\mathbf{U}_h^{n + 1} = \frac{1}{3} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{2}{3} \left[ \mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} \right) \right]. \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.label: RK

nodes.name: OEDG scheme (OE procedure after each RK stage)
nodes.statement: To eliminate the oscillations and enforce stability, we apply the OE procedure \cite{peng2023oedg} following each RK stage, leading to \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1} &= \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}^{n}_h \right), & \mathbf{U}^{n, 1}_h &= \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1}, \\ \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2} &= \frac{3}{4} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{1}{4} \left( \mathbf{U}^{n, 1}_h + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}^{n, 1}_h ) \right), & \mathbf{U}^{n, 2}_h &= \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2}, \\ \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3} & = \frac{1}{3} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{2}{3} \left( \mathbf{U}^{n, 2}_h + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}^{n, 2}_h ) \right), & \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h & = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3}, & \mathbf{U}^{n+1}_h & = \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h. \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: Apply the OE operator $\mathcal{F}_\tau$ after each SSP-RK stage.

nodes.name: OEDG RK stages (3.4)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1} &= \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}^{n}_h \right), & \mathbf{U}^{n, 1}_h &= \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1}, \\ \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2} &= \frac{3}{4} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{1}{4} \left( \mathbf{U}^{n, 1}_h + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}^{n, 1}_h ) \right), & \mathbf{U}^{n, 2}_h &= \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2}, \\ \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3} & = \frac{1}{3} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{2}{3} \left( \mathbf{U}^{n, 2}_h + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}^{n, 2}_h ) \right), & \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h & = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3}, & \mathbf{U}^{n+1}_h & = \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h. \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.label: OEOperator

nodes.name: Oscillation-eliminating (OE) operator
nodes.statement: Here, the OE operator $\mathcal{F}_\tau: \mathbb{V}_h^k \rightarrow \mathbb{V}_h^k$ is the solution operator of the following damping equation \eqref{InitialValueProblem}. Specifically, we define $(\mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,s}) (x) = \mathbf{U}_\sigma (x, \tau)$, where $\mathbf{U}_\sigma (x, \hat{t})$ is the solution of the following ordinary differential equation with respect to $\hat{t}$: \begin{equation} \left\{ \begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \hat{t}} \int_{I_j} \mathbf{U}_{\sigma} \cdot \bm{\phi} \, \mathrm{d} x + \sum_{i = 0}^{k} \theta_j \frac{\sigma_j^{i} \big( \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,s} \big)}{\Delta x} \int_{I_j} \left( \mathbf{U}_{\sigma} - \mathcal{P}^{i - 1}_{\sigma} \mathbf{U}_{\sigma} \right) \cdot \bm{\phi} \, \mathrm{d} x = 0, \\ & \mathbf{U}_{\sigma} (x, 0) = \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,s} (x), \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation} where $\bm{\phi} \in (\mathbb{P}^k ( I_j ))^3$ is a test function, $\theta_j$ is the spectral radius of the Jacobian matrix $\partial \mathbf{F} \big( \overline{\mathbf{U}}_j^n \big) / \partial \mathbf{U}$, and $\mathcal{P}^{\, i}_\sigma$ is the standard $L^2$ projection operator.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: $\mathcal{F}_\tau$ is the time-$\tau$ solution operator of a modal damping ODE driven by jump-based coefficients.

nodes.name: OE damping equation (3.5)
nodes.statement: \left\{ \begin{aligned} & \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d} \hat{t}} \int_{I_j} \mathbf{U}_{\sigma} \cdot \bm{\phi} \, \mathrm{d} x + \sum_{i = 0}^{k} \theta_j \frac{\sigma_j^{i} \big( \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,s} \big)}{\Delta x} \int_{I_j} \left( \mathbf{U}_{\sigma} - \mathcal{P}^{i - 1}_{\sigma} \mathbf{U}_{\sigma} \right) \cdot \bm{\phi} \, \mathrm{d} x = 0, \\ & \mathbf{U}_{\sigma} (x, 0) = \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,s} (x), \end{aligned} \right.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.label: InitialValueProblem

nodes.name: Scale-invariant damping coefficients
nodes.statement: To make sure that the OE operator $\mathcal{F}_\tau$ is both scale-invariant and evolution-invariant (see \cite{peng2023oedg}), the damping coefficient $\sigma^i_j \big( \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, s} \big)$ is defined as $ \sigma^i_j \big( \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, s} \big) := \max \left\{ \sigma^i_j \left( \tilde \rho_h^{n,s} \right), \sigma^i_j \left( \tilde y_h^{n,s} \right), \sigma^i_j \left( \tilde z_h^{n,s} \right) \right\} $ with $\widetilde {\mathbf{U}}^{n,s}_h(x) = \big(\tilde \rho_h^{n,s}(x),$ $\tilde y_h^{n,s}(x), \tilde z_h^{n,s}(x)\big)^\top$ and \begin{equation*} \sigma_j^i (u) = \left\{ \begin{aligned} & 0, \quad && {\rm if} \; u \equiv \mathrm{constant}, \\ & \frac{(2 i + 1) (\Delta x)^i}{(2 k - 1) \, i !} \cdot \frac { \left \vert [\![ \partial^i_x u ]\!]_{j - \frac{1}{2}} \right \vert + \left \vert [\![ \partial^i_x u ]\!]_{j + \frac{1}{2}} \right \vert } { 2 \left \Vert u - \frac{1}{\vert \mathcal{D} \vert} \int_{\mathcal{D}} u(x) \, \mathrm{d} x \right \Vert _{L^\infty (\mathcal{D})} } , \quad && {\rm otherwise}. \end{aligned} \right. \end{equation*} Here, $\mathcal{D}$ denotes the computational domain, and $[\![ u ]\!]_{j+\frac12} = u_{j + \frac{1}{2}}^+ - u_{j + \frac{1}{2}}^-$ denotes the jump of $u$ at the cell interface $x = x_{j + \frac{1}{2}}$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: Damping coefficients from normalized interface jumps of derivatives, maximized over components.

nodes.name: Explicit solution of the OE damping equation
nodes.statement: The explicit solution of \eqref{InitialValueProblem} was found in \cite{peng2023oedg}: \begin{equation*} \mathbf{U}^{n,s} = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,s} = \sum_{j} \mathbbm{1}_{I_j}(x) \left[ \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_j^{[0]} \phi_j^{[0]} (x) + \sum^k_{i = 1} \exp\Bigg( - \frac{ \tau \theta_j}{\Delta x} \sum_{q = 0}^i \sigma_j^q \big( \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, s} \big) \Bigg) \widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_j^{[i]} \phi_j^{[i]} (x) \right] . \end{equation*} Here, $\widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_j^{[i]}$ is the $i$-th modal coefficient of $\widetilde {\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, s}$ in $I_j$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: The OE operator keeps the 0-th mode and damps the $i$-th modal coefficient by an explicit exponential factor.

nodes.name: Justification of Proposition 3.1
nodes.statement: Please note that the $0$-th mode is not affected by the OE operator, leading to the following proposition.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: The explicit OE solution leaves the 0-th mode (the cell average) untouched.

nodes.name: OE operator preserves cell averages
nodes.statement: Applying the OE operator to a numerical solution maintains its cell averages, that is, $\overline{\mathbf{U}}^{n,s}_j = \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,s}_j$, for $j = 1,\dots,N_x$ and $s = 1,2,3$.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: The OE procedure does not change cell averages.
conclusions: Applying the OE operator to a numerical solution maintains its cell averages
nodes.label: lem:1625b

nodes.name: OE procedure versus TVB limiter
nodes.statement: We adopt the OE procedure instead of the traditional TVB limiter to control numerical oscillations. The main reason for this choice is that while the TVB limiter requires the solution to be decomposed into its characteristics for an effective simulation, the OE procedure does not necessitate such a decomposition. For more information on OEDG methods, readers are referred to \cite{peng2023oedg}.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: OE is preferred over TVB limiting since it needs no characteristic decomposition.

nodes.name: OE operator preserves order of accuracy
nodes.statement: Adding the OE operator to the scheme \eqref{RK} does not change its order of accuracy; see \cite{peng2023oedg}.
nodes.section: 3 High-order OEDG methods for ARZ models

nodes.name: BP-OEDG scheme
nodes.statement: To enforce this BP property, we add a BP limiter to the numerical solution following each OE procedure in \eqref{OEOperator}, resulting in \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} &\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1} = \mathbf{U}^{n}_h + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}^{n}_h \right), & \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1} & = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1}, & \mathbf{U}_j^{n, 1} & = \mathcal{B} \left( \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n, 1}; {\Omega}_j^{n,1} \right) \; \forall j, \\ & \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2} = \frac{3}{4} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{1}{4} \left( \mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} ) \right), & \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2} & = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2}, & \mathbf{U}_j^{n, 2} & = \mathcal{B} \left( \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n, 2}; {\Omega}_j^{n,2} \right) \; \forall j, \\ &\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3} = \frac{1}{3} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{2}{3} \left( \mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} ) \right), & \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3} & = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3}, & \mathbf{U}_j^{n,3} & = \mathcal{B} \left( \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n,3}; {\Omega}_j^{n,3} \right) \; \forall j, \\ &\mathbf{U}^{n+1}_h = \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h. \end{aligned} \end{equation} Here, $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_j$ (resp. $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}^{n,s}_j$) denotes the local polynomials of numerical solution $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_h$ (resp. $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}^{n,s}_h$) in $I_j$, $\mathcal{B}$ denotes the BP limiter, which modifies the local polynomial $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n,s}$, such that the resulting local polynomial ${\mathbf{U}}_j^{n,s}$ satisfies the invariant domain ${\Omega}_j^{n,s}$.
nodes.section: 4 High-order BP-OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.statement_short: OEDG scheme with the BP limiter $\mathcal{B}$ applied after each OE step to enforce the approximate invariant domain $\Omega_j^{n,s}$.

nodes.name: BP-OEDG RK stages (4.1)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1} = \mathbf{U}^{n}_h + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} \left(\mathbf{U}^{n}_h \right), & \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1} & = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 1}, & \mathbf{U}_j^{n, 1} & = \mathcal{B} \left( \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n, 1}; {\Omega}_j^{n,1} \right) \; \forall j, \\ & \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2} = \frac{3}{4} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{1}{4} \left( \mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 1} ) \right), & \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2} & = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n, 2}, & \mathbf{U}_j^{n, 2} & = \mathcal{B} \left( \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n, 2}; {\Omega}_j^{n,2} \right) \; \forall j, \\ &\widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3} = \frac{1}{3} \mathbf{U}_h^{n} + \frac{2}{3} \left( \mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} + \Delta t_n \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}_h^{n, 2} ) \right), & \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3} & = \mathcal{F}_\tau \widetilde{\mathbf{U}}_h^{n,3}, & \mathbf{U}_j^{n,3} & = \mathcal{B} \left( \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n,3}; {\Omega}_j^{n,3} \right) \; \forall j, \\ &\mathbf{U}^{n+1}_h = \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h. \end{aligned}
nodes.section: 4 High-order BP-OEDG methods for ARZ models
nodes.label: BPOE

nodes.name: Stage-index convention
nodes.statement: For notational convenience, we consider the time level $t_n$ as the final (resp. initial) stage of preceding (resp. following) RK step, that is, $\mathbf{U}^{n-1,3}_h = \mathbf{U}^n_h = \mathbf{U}^{n,0}_h$ and $\Omega_j^{n-1,3} = \Omega_j^n = \Omega_j^{n,0}$ for all $j$.

nodes.name: Approximate initial global invariant domain Omega^0
nodes.statement: At the beginning of computation, we estimate the initial global invariant domain \[ {\Omega}^{0} = \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z > 0, w \in \left[ (w_{\min})^{0}, (w_{\max})^{0} \right] \\ v \ge (v_{\min})^{0}, c \in \left[ (c_{\min})^{0}, (c_{\max})^{0} \right] \end{array} \right\} \] by sampling $\mathbf{U}_h^0(x)$ over a uniform auxiliary mesh $\big\{x^{\rm s}_i\big\}_{i = 1}^{N_{\rm s}}$: \begin{gather} (v_{\min})^0 = \max \Big\{ \min_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} v\left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) - \varepsilon_0, 0 \Big\}, \\ (w_{\min})^0 = \min_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} w \left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) - \varepsilon_0, \qquad (w_{\max})^0 = \max_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} w \left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) + \varepsilon_0, \\ (c_{\min})^0 = \min_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} c \left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) - \varepsilon_0, \qquad (c_{\max})^0 = \max_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} c \left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) + \varepsilon_0. \end{gather}
nodes.statement_short: Initial bounds of $v,w,c$ estimated by sampling the initial DG solution on a fine mesh, relaxed by $\varepsilon_0$.

nodes.name: Initial bound of v (4.2)
nodes.statement: (v_{\min})^0 = \max \Big\{ \min_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} v\left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) - \varepsilon_0, 0 \Big\},
nodes.label: eq:1769a

nodes.name: Initial bounds of w (4.3)
nodes.statement: (w_{\min})^0 = \min_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} w \left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) - \varepsilon_0, \qquad (w_{\max})^0 = \max_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} w \left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) + \varepsilon_0,
nodes.label: eq:1769b

nodes.name: Initial bounds of c (4.4)
nodes.statement: (c_{\min})^0 = \min_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} c \left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) - \varepsilon_0, \qquad (c_{\max})^0 = \max_{i = 1,\dots,N_s} c \left(\mathbf{U}_h^0 (x_i^{\rm s})\right) + \varepsilon_0.
nodes.label: eq:1769c

nodes.name: Relaxation parameter epsilon_0
nodes.statement: The approximate global invariant domain $\Omega^0$ may not be identical to the exact global invariant domain $\Omega$. If $\Omega \backslash \Omega^0 \neq \emptyset$, enforcing BP property with respect to $\Omega^0$ may be overly strict: a reference solution with its range overlapping $\Omega \backslash \Omega^0$ may be subject to (unnecessary) modifications by the BP limiter, which may lead to accuracy degeneracy in the numerical results. To avoid such an issue, we introduce a small positive parameter $\varepsilon_0$ in the above formulas \eqref{eq:1769a}--\eqref{eq:1769c} to slightly expand $\Omega^{0}$. In all the numerical experiments reported in \Cref{sec:num}, we set $\varepsilon_0 = 10^{-9}$.
nodes.statement_short: $\Omega^0$ is enlarged by $\varepsilon_0=10^{-9}$ to avoid over-strict limiting and accuracy loss.

nodes.name: Approximate global invariant domains Omega^{n,s}
nodes.statement: We update the approximate global invariant domain using the following formula \begin{equation} \Omega^{n,s} := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z > 0, w \in \left[ (w_{\min})^{n,s}, (w_{\max})^{n,s} \right] \\ v \ge (v_{\min})^{n,s}, c \in \left[ (c_{\min})^{n,s}, (c_{\max})^{n,s} \right] \end{array} \right\} \end{equation} with \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} (v_{\min})^{n,s} & = \min \big\{ (v_{\min})^{n,s-1},v\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),v\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \\ (w_{\min})^{n,s} & = \min \big\{ (w_{\min})^{n,s-1},w\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),w\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \\ (w_{\max})^{n,s} & = \max \big\{ (w_{\max})^{n,s-1},w\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),w\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \\ (c_{\min})^{n,s} & = \min \big\{ (c_{\min})^{n,s-1},c\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),c\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \\ (c_{\max})^{n,s} & = \max \big\{ (c_{\max})^{n,s-1},c\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),c\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} where $\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})$ and $\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})$ denote respectively the states immediate outside the left and right boundaries, which are determined by boundary conditions.
nodes.statement_short: Global bounds updated each stage by including the boundary states given by boundary conditions.

nodes.name: Global invariant domain Omega^{n,s} (4.5)
nodes.statement: \Omega^{n,s} := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z > 0, w \in \left[ (w_{\min})^{n,s}, (w_{\max})^{n,s} \right] \\ v \ge (v_{\min})^{n,s}, c \in \left[ (c_{\min})^{n,s}, (c_{\max})^{n,s} \right] \end{array} \right\}
nodes.label: eq:1795

nodes.name: Global bound updates (4.6)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} (v_{\min})^{n,s} & = \min \big\{ (v_{\min})^{n,s-1},v\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),v\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \\ (w_{\min})^{n,s} & = \min \big\{ (w_{\min})^{n,s-1},w\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),w\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \\ (w_{\max})^{n,s} & = \max \big\{ (w_{\max})^{n,s-1},w\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),w\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \\ (c_{\min})^{n,s} & = \min \big\{ (c_{\min})^{n,s-1},c\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),c\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \\ (c_{\max})^{n,s} & = \max \big\{ (c_{\max})^{n,s-1},c\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-})\big),c\big(\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+})\big) \big\}, \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:1807

nodes.name: Boundary states lie in the global invariant domain
nodes.statement: The global invariants defined in \eqref{eq:1795}--\eqref{eq:1807} satisfy $\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-}) \in \Omega^{n,s}$ and $\mathbf{U}^{n,s-1}_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,s}$.
nodes.label: lem:1872

nodes.name: Justification of Proposition 4.2
nodes.statement: Based on the formulas in \eqref{eq:1807}, the global invariant domains corresponding to all time steps and RK stages form a series of nested domains.
nodes.statement_short: The update formulas only take min/max with previous bounds, so the domains are nested.

nodes.name: Nestedness of global invariant domains
nodes.statement: The global invariants defined in \eqref{eq:1795}--\eqref{eq:1807} satisfy $\Omega^{n_1,s_1} \subseteq \Omega^{n_2,s_2}$ and $\Omega^{n_1} \subseteq \Omega^{n_2}$ for any $0 \le n_1 \le n_2$ and $0\le s_1 \le s_2\le 3$.
assumptions: for any $0 \le n_1 \le n_2$ and $0\le s_1 \le s_2\le 3$
nodes.label: lem:1889

nodes.name: Approximate local invariant domains Omega_j^{n,s}
nodes.statement: We express the approximate local invariant domain on $I_j$ at the $s$-th RK stage of the $n$-th time step by \begin{equation} \Omega^{n,s}_j := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z>0, w \in \left[ (w_{\min})^{n,s}_j, (w_{\max})^{n,s}_j \right] \\ v \ge (v_{\min})^{n,s}_j, c \in \left[ (c_{\min})^{n,s}_j, (c_{\max})^{n,s}_j \right] \end{array} \right\} \end{equation} which is defined by the following formulas \begin{equation} \Omega^{n,1}_j := \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{j,*}, \quad \Omega^{n,s}_j := \Omega^{n,s} \cap \left( \Omega^{n,s-1}_{j} \cup \Omega^{n,s-1}_{j,*} \right) ~~ \textrm{for} ~~ s = 2,3, \end{equation} where \begin{equation} \Omega^{n,s}_{j,*} := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z > 0, v \ge (v_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}-\sqrt{\Delta x} \, \big|(v_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big| \\ w \in \left[ (w_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}-\sqrt{\Delta x} \,\big|(w_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big|, (w_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}+\sqrt{\Delta x} \,\big|(w_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big| \right] \\ c \in \left[ (c_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}-\sqrt{\Delta x} \,\big|(c_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big|, (c_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}+\sqrt{\Delta x} \,\big|(c_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big| \right] \end{array} \right\}. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Local domains intersect the global domain with $\sqrt{\Delta x}$-relaxed local bounds from the previous stage.

nodes.name: Local invariant domain (4.7)
nodes.statement: \Omega^{n,s}_j := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z>0, w \in \left[ (w_{\min})^{n,s}_j, (w_{\max})^{n,s}_j \right] \\ v \ge (v_{\min})^{n,s}_j, c \in \left[ (c_{\min})^{n,s}_j, (c_{\max})^{n,s}_j \right] \end{array} \right\}
nodes.label: eq:1851

nodes.name: Recursive local domains (4.8)
nodes.statement: \Omega^{n,1}_j := \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{j,*}, \quad \Omega^{n,s}_j := \Omega^{n,s} \cap \left( \Omega^{n,s-1}_{j} \cup \Omega^{n,s-1}_{j,*} \right) ~~ \textrm{for} ~~ s = 2,3,
nodes.label: eq:1917

nodes.name: Relaxed local domain Omega_{j,*} (4.9)
nodes.statement: \Omega^{n,s}_{j,*} := \left\{ \mathbf{U} \in \mathbb{R}^3 : \begin{array}{r} \rho > 0, z > 0, v \ge (v_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}-\sqrt{\Delta x} \, \big|(v_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big| \\ w \in \left[ (w_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}-\sqrt{\Delta x} \,\big|(w_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big|, (w_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}+\sqrt{\Delta x} \,\big|(w_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big| \right] \\ c \in \left[ (c_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}-\sqrt{\Delta x} \,\big|(c_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big|, (c_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}+\sqrt{\Delta x} \,\big|(c_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}\big| \right] \end{array} \right\}.
nodes.label: eq:1927

nodes.name: Local bound estimates of v, w, c
nodes.statement: Here, $(v_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}$, $(w_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}$, $(w_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}$, $(c_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*}$, $(c_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*}$ are respectively estimates of minimum/maximum of $v$, $w$, and $c$ of intermediate solution $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_h$ in the vicinity of $I_j$: \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} (v_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \min\Big\{ \min\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} v\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \min\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} v\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), v\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), v\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \\ (w_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \min\Big\{ \min\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} w\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \min\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} w\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), w\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), w\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \\ (w_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \max\Big\{ \max\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} w\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \max\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} w\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), w\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), w\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \\ (c_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \min\Big\{ \min\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} c\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \min\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} c\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), c\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), c\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \\ (c_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \max\Big\{ \max\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} c\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \max\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} c\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), c\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), c\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \end{aligned} \end{equation} Here, $\mathcal{C}: C(I_j) \mapsto \mathbb{P}^3(I_j)$ denotes a cubic interpolation operator over $I_j$, such that $[\mathcal{C}f](x) = f(x)$ for $x \in \big\{x_{j-\frac12},x_{j-\frac16},x_{j+\frac16},x_{j+\frac12}\big\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Local min/max of $v,w,c$ from Gauss-Lobatto values, a cubic interpolant, and neighbouring interface values.

nodes.name: Local bound estimates (4.10)
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} (v_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \min\Big\{ \min\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} v\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \min\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} v\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), v\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), v\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \\ (w_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \min\Big\{ \min\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} w\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \min\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} w\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), w\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), w\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \\ (w_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \max\Big\{ \max\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} w\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \max\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} w\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), w\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), w\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \\ (c_{\min})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \min\Big\{ \min\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} c\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \min\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} c\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), c\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), c\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \\ (c_{\max})^{n,s}_{j,*} & = \max\Big\{ \max\limits_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} c\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x_{j,\ell}^{\tt GL})\big), \max\limits_{I_j} \mathcal{C} c\big(\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}\big), c\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+})\big), c\big(\mathbf{U}_h^{n,s}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-})\big) \Big\}, \end{aligned}
nodes.label: eq:1982

nodes.name: Local domain is stricter than global
nodes.statement: Based on the formulas in \eqref{eq:1917}, please note that for $s = 1,2,3$, it holds that $\Omega^{n,s}_j \subseteq \Omega^{n,s}$, that is, the local invariant domain $\Omega^{n,s}_j$ always imposes a stronger restriction on the numerical solutions than the global one $\Omega^{n,s}$.

nodes.name: Relaxation of local bounds by sqrt(Delta x)
nodes.statement: If the approximate invariant domain is too strict, enforcing such an invariant domain upon a numerical solution may lead to accuracy degeneracy. To avoid such an issue, we expand the local invariant domains in \eqref{eq:1927} by relaxing the upper and lower bounds with a multiplicative factor of $\sqrt{\Delta x}$.

nodes.name: Constraint functions H_1,...,H_7
nodes.statement: In fact, the constraints shown in the definition of these domains can be equivalently expressed by the positivities of the following functions: \begin{align*} & H_1(\mathbf{U}) := \rho, \; H_2(\mathbf{U}) := z, \; H_{3}(\mathbf{U}) := \rho \big( w - (w_{\min})^{n,s}_j \big), \; H_{4}(\mathbf{U}) := \rho \big( (w_{\max})^{n,s}_j - w \big), \\ & H_{5}(\mathbf{U}) := \rho \big( c - (c_{\min})^{n,s}_j \big), \; H_{6}(\mathbf{U}) := \rho \big( (c_{\max})^{n,s}_j - c \big), \; H_7(\mathbf{U}) := \rho \big(v-(v_{\min})_j^{n,s}\big). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Invariant-domain constraints rewritten as positivity of seven functions $H_r$.

nodes.name: Concavity of the constraint functions H_r
nodes.statement: Here, the functions $H_1,\dots,H_6$ are all linear, and thus concave. The function $H_7$ is also concave for $\mathbf{U} \in \Omega_0$, since it can be rewritten as a sum of concave functions: $H_7(\mathbf{U}) = y + \rho v_{\min} - \rho (v_{\min})_j^{n,s} - \eta(\rho,z)$. The function $\eta$ was defined in \eqref{eq:406}, and its convexity was shown in the proof of \Cref{lem:466}.
conclusions: the functions $H_1,\dots,H_6$ are all linear, and thus concave

nodes.name: Local scaling form
nodes.statement: Before introducing the BP limiter $\mathcal{B}$, we first review several properties of local scaling form $\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) := \theta \widehat{\mathbf{U}} + (1-\theta) \overline{\mathbf{U}}$, which has been used intensively in constructing BP limiters, for example, in \cite{zhang2011maximum,zhang2010maximum}.

nodes.name: Properties of local scaling for concave constraints
nodes.statement: For any $d \in \mathbb{N}^+$, consider a convex set $\mathcal{R} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, a continuous and concave function $H(\mathbf{U}): \mathcal{R} \mapsto \mathbb{R}$, and a threshold $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon := \{\mathbf{U} \in \mathcal{R} : H(\mathbf{U}) \ge \varepsilon \}$ is not empty. For any $\overline{\mathbf{U}} \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ and $\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \in \mathcal{R}$, let us define \[ \Theta(\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}},H,\varepsilon) := \begin{dcases} 1 & \textrm{if }H(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) \ge \varepsilon, \\ \textrm{ the unique solution of } H\big(\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\big) = \varepsilon \textrm{ in } [0,1] & \textrm{if }H(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) < \varepsilon. \end{dcases} \] where $\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) := \theta \widehat{\mathbf{U}} + (1-\theta) \overline{\mathbf{U}}$. It holds that (i) the set $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ is convex; (ii) the equation $H\big(\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\big) = \varepsilon$ has a unique solution in $[0,1]$ for $\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \not \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$; and (iii) for any $\theta \in \big[0,\Theta(\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}},H,\varepsilon)\big]$, $\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$, that is, $H(\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}})) \ge \varepsilon$.
nodes.statement_short: For concave $H$, the superlevel set is convex, the scaling equation has a unique root $\Theta$, and any $\theta\le\Theta$ keeps $H\ge\varepsilon$.
assumptions: consider a convex set $\mathcal{R} \in \mathbb{R}^d$, a continuous and concave function $H(\mathbf{U}): \mathcal{R} \mapsto \mathbb{R}$, and a threshold $\varepsilon \in \mathbb{R}$ such that $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon := \{\mathbf{U} \in \mathcal{R} : H(\mathbf{U}) \ge \varepsilon \}$ is not empty
conclusions: (ii) the equation $H\big(\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\big) = \varepsilon$ has a unique solution in $[0,1]$ for $\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \not \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$
nodes.label: lem:1467

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.3
nodes.statement: (i) For any $\lambda \in [0,1]$ and any $\mathbf{U}_0$, $\mathbf{U}_1 \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon \subseteq \mathcal{R}$, the convexity of $\mathcal{R}$ implies that $\mathbf{U}_\lambda = \lambda \mathbf{U}_1 + (1-\lambda) \mathbf{U}_0 \in \mathcal{R}$. Due to the concavity of function $H$, it holds that $H(\mathbf{U}_\lambda) \ge \lambda H(\mathbf{U}_1) + (1-\lambda) H(\mathbf{U}_0) \ge \varepsilon$. Therefore, $\mathbf{U}_\lambda \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ and $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ is convex. (ii) For $\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \not \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$, the set $\{\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) : \theta \in [0,1]\}$ forms a line segment connecting $\overline{\mathbf{U}} \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ and $\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \not \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$. This line segment has to intersect with the boundary of $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$, namely, $\{\mathbf{U}\in\mathcal{R}:H(\mathbf{U}) = \varepsilon\}$ and the convexity of $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ also implies that the intersection happens only once. The claim (ii) is proven. (iii) Since $\mathbf{U}_0 = \overline{\mathbf{U}} \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ and $\mathcal{U}(\Theta(\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}},H,\varepsilon);\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$, the convexity of $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ immediately implies (iii).
nodes.statement_short: Concavity gives convexity of the superlevel set; a segment leaving a convex set crosses its boundary once.

nodes.name: BP limiter B
nodes.statement: Now, We introduce the BP limiter $\mathcal{B}$, which consists of two steps: \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),leftmargin=6mm] \item[\textbf{Step 1}:] Enforce the positivity of $\rho$ and $z$ by a local scaling \begin{equation} \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x) = \Big( \theta_1 \hat\rho_j^{n,s}(x) +(1-\theta_1)\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.4 pt}{$\bar{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.4 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho_j^{n,s}, \hat y_j^{n,s}(x), \theta_2 \hat z_j^{n,s}(x) +(1-\theta_2)\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.4 pt}{$\bar{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.4 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z_j^{n,s} \Big)^\top, \end{equation} where the local scaling coefficients $\{\theta_r\}_{r = 1}^2$ are defined by \[ \theta_r = \min_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} \Theta\Big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_r,\varepsilon_r\Big), \;\; \varepsilon_r = \min \Big\{ 10^{-12} , H_r(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s}) \Big\},\; r = 1,2. \] Here, the $L$-point Gauss--Lobatto nodes in $I_j$ are denoted by $\{x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell} \}_{\ell = 1}^L$, and the positive parameter $\varepsilon_r$ is introduced to enhance the robustness of above limiter under the influence of round-off errors. Also, please note that the local scaling \eqref{eq:1706} does not change the cell average, that is, $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s} = \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}$. \item[\textbf{Step 2}:]Enforce the remaining constraints by \begin{equation} \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s}(x) = \theta_3 \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x) + (1-\theta_3) \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}, \end{equation} where the local scaling coefficients $\theta_3$ is defined by \[ \theta_3 = \min_{r = 3,\dots,7} \min_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} \Theta\Big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_r,\varepsilon_r\Big), \; \varepsilon_r = \min \Big\{ 10^{-12} , H_r(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s}) \Big\},\; r = 3,\dots,7. \] The local scaling \eqref{eq:1733} does not change the cell average: $\overline{\mathbf{U}}_{j}^{n,s} = \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s} = \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}$. \end{enumerate}
nodes.statement_short: Two-step Zhang-Shu-type scaling limiter: scale $\rho,z$ toward the cell average for positivity, then scale the whole polynomial to satisfy $H_3,\dots,H_7\ge\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Positivity scaling (4.11)
nodes.statement: \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x) = \Big( \theta_1 \hat\rho_j^{n,s}(x) +(1-\theta_1)\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.4 pt}{$\bar{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.4 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho_j^{n,s}, \hat y_j^{n,s}(x), \theta_2 \hat z_j^{n,s}(x) +(1-\theta_2)\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.4 pt}{$\bar{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.4 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z_j^{n,s} \Big)^\top,
nodes.label: eq:1706

nodes.name: Remaining-constraint scaling (4.12)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s}(x) = \theta_3 \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x) + (1-\theta_3) \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s},
nodes.label: eq:1733

nodes.name: BP limiter enforces the invariant domain at Gauss-Lobatto nodes
nodes.statement: If the local polynomial $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}^{n,s}_j$ satisfies $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,s}_j \in \Omega^{n,s}_j$, then the result of the BP limiter, $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_j = \mathcal{B}\big(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}^{n,s}_j;\Omega^{n,s}_j\big)$, satisfies $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,s}_j$, $\ell = 1,\dots,L$.
nodes.statement_short: If the cell average lies in $\Omega_j^{n,s}$, the limited polynomial lies in it at all Gauss-Lobatto nodes.
assumptions: the local polynomial $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}^{n,s}_j$ satisfies $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,s}_j \in \Omega^{n,s}_j$
nodes.label: lem:1775

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.4
nodes.statement: Let us consider an arbitrary $\ell \in \{1,\dots,L\}$. Notice that $H_1(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.4 pt}{$\bar{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.4 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho_j^{n,s}) \ge \varepsilon_1$ and $H_1(\cdot)$ is concave in $\mathbb{R}^3$, \Cref{lem:1467} implies $\hat{\rho}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) = H_1\big(\mathcal{U}(\theta_1;\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}))\big) \ge \varepsilon_1$, since $0 \le \theta_1 \le \Theta\big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_1,\varepsilon_1\big)$. Similarly, we can prove that $\hat{z}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \ge \varepsilon_2$. Therefore, $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega_0$ and $\Theta\big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_r,\varepsilon_r\big) = 1$ for $r = 1,2$. Let us consider an arbitrary $r \in \{1,\dots,7\}$. Since $H_r(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s}) = H_r(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}) \ge \varepsilon_r$, $H_r(\cdot)$ is concave in $\Omega_0$, and $0 \le \theta_3 \le \Theta\big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_r,\varepsilon_r\big)$ , \Cref{lem:1467} implies $ H_r\big( \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \big) = H_r\big(\mathcal{U}(\theta_3;\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}))\big) \ge \varepsilon_r$, that is, $\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega_{j}^{n,s}$.
nodes.statement_short: Apply Lemma 4.3 to $H_1,H_2$ (step 1) and then to the concave $H_3,\dots,H_7$ on $\Omega_0$ (step 2).

nodes.name: Newton's method for Theta
nodes.statement: When evaluating the function $\Theta$, if the equation $H\big(\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\big) = \varepsilon$ has no explicit solution, we employ the Newton's method to solve it numerically.

nodes.name: BP limiter preserves order of accuracy
nodes.statement: Applying the BP limiter $\mathcal{B}$ defined in \eqref{eq:1706}--\eqref{eq:1733} to a numerical solution maintains its original order of accuracy; see \cite{wu2021minimum,zhang2011maximum,zhang2010maximum}.

nodes.name: Forward Euler step
nodes.statement: We first focus on a single forward Euler (FE) time step: $\mathbf{U}_h^* = \mathbf{U}_h + \Delta t \mathcal{L} (\mathbf{U}_h)$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes

nodes.name: FE cell-average update (4.13)
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathbf{U}}^*_j = \overline{\mathbf{U}}_j + \frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x} \left[ \widehat{\mathbf{F}}(\mathbf{U}_{j-\frac12}^{-},\mathbf{U}_{j-\frac12}^{+}) - \widehat{\mathbf{F}}(\mathbf{U}_{j+\frac12}^{-},\mathbf{U}_{j+\frac12}^{+}) \right].
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.label: eq:2121

nodes.name: BP property of forward Euler step
nodes.statement: Considering an invariant domain $\Omega$ in the form of \eqref{eq:270}, if $\mathbf{U}^{-}_{j-\frac12} \in \Omega$, $\mathbf{U}^{+}_{j+\frac12} \in \Omega$, $\mathbf{U}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega$ for any $\ell = 1,\dots,L$, then the result of the FE step \eqref{eq:2121} with \[ \alpha \ge \max \big\{ \alpha_{\max}(\mathbf{U}^{-}_{j-\frac12},\mathbf{U}^{+}_{j-\frac12}), \alpha_{\max}(\mathbf{U}^{-}_{j+\frac12},\mathbf{U}^{+}_{j+\frac12}) \big\} \] satisfies $\overline{\mathbf{U}}^*_j \in \Omega$, under the CFL condition \begin{equation} \alpha \frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x} \le \omega^{\tt GL}_1. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Under the CFL condition and $\alpha\ge\alpha_{max}$, an FE step keeps the cell average in $\Omega$ if interface and Gauss-Lobatto values are in $\Omega$.
assumptions: Considering an invariant domain $\Omega$ in the form of \eqref{eq:270}
nodes.label: lem:2154

nodes.name: CFL condition (4.14)
nodes.statement: \alpha \frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x} \le \omega^{\tt GL}_1.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.label: eq:2300

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 4.5
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbf{U}_j(x) \in \mathbb{P}^k$, the $L$-point Gauss--Lobatto quadrature holds exactly: \[ \overline{\mathbf{U}}_j = \frac{1}{\Delta x} \int_{I_j} \mathbf{U}_j(x) \, \textrm{d}x = \sum_{\ell = 1}^L \omega^{\tt GL}_\ell \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}). \] Since $\omega^{\tt GL}_1 = \omega^{\tt GL}_L$, $x^{\tt GL}_{j,1} = x_{j-\frac12}$, $x^{\tt GL}_{j,L} = x_{j+\frac12}$, we can rewrite \eqref{eq:2121} as \begin{equation} \overline{\mathbf{U}}^*_j = \sum_{\ell = 2}^L \omega^{\tt GL}_\ell \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) + (\omega^{\tt GL}_1-\lambda) \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,1}) + (\omega^{\tt GL}_1-\lambda) \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,L}) + \lambda \mathbf{U}_j^{-} + \lambda \mathbf{U}_j^{+}, \end{equation} where $\lambda := \alpha \frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x} \le \omega^{\tt GL}_1$, and $\mathbf{U}_j^{\pm} := \mathcal{S}_{\tt GLF}(\mathbf{U}^{\pm}_{j-\frac12},\mathbf{U}^{\pm}_{j+\frac12})$. \Cref{thm:1471} implies that $\mathbf{U}^{\pm}_j \in \Omega$. The convex combination \eqref{eq:2265} implies that $\overline{\mathbf{U}}^*_j \in \Omega$ due to the convexity of $\Omega$ (\Cref{lem:466}). The proof is completed.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Write the FE cell average as a convex combination of Gauss-Lobatto values and GLF states, then use Theorem 2.6 and convexity of $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Convex decomposition of FE update (4.15)
nodes.statement: \overline{\mathbf{U}}^*_j = \sum_{\ell = 2}^L \omega^{\tt GL}_\ell \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) + (\omega^{\tt GL}_1-\lambda) \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,1}) + (\omega^{\tt GL}_1-\lambda) \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,L}) + \lambda \mathbf{U}_j^{-} + \lambda \mathbf{U}_j^{+},
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.label: eq:2265

nodes.name: Global BP property of BP-OEDG scheme
nodes.statement: If the global invariant domains $\Omega^{n,s}$ defined in \eqref{eq:1795}--\eqref{eq:1807} are considered, then the scheme \eqref{BPOE} with $\alpha \ge \max_j \alpha_{\max}(\mathbf{U}^-_{j+\frac12},\mathbf{U}^+_{j+\frac12})$ and under the CFL condition \eqref{eq:2300} is globally BP, namely, \begin{equation} \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n} ~~ \forall j ~ \forall \ell ~~ \Longrightarrow ~~ \mathbf{U}^{n+1}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n+1} ~~ \forall j ~ \forall \ell. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: With global invariant domains, the BP-OEDG scheme keeps Gauss-Lobatto values in $\Omega^n$ from step to step under the CFL condition.
assumptions: the global invariant domains $\Omega^{n,s}$ defined in \eqref{eq:1795}--\eqref{eq:1807} are considered
with $\alpha \ge \max_j \alpha_{\max}(\mathbf{U}^-_{j+\frac12},\mathbf{U}^+_{j+\frac12})$ and under the CFL condition \eqref{eq:2300}
nodes.label: lem:2350

nodes.name: Global BP property (4.16)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n} ~~ \forall j ~ \forall \ell ~~ \Longrightarrow ~~ \mathbf{U}^{n+1}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n+1} ~~ \forall j ~ \forall \ell.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.label: eq:2177

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.6
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbf{U}_j^n \in (\mathbb{P}^k)^3$ for all $j$, the $L$-point Gauss--Lobatto quadrature holds exactly, namely, $ \overline{\mathbf{U}}_j^n = \frac{1}{\Delta x} \int_{I_j} \mathbf{U}^n_j(x) \, \textrm{d} x = \sum_{\ell = 1}^{L} \omega^{\tt GL} \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}), $ which decomposes $\overline{\mathbf{U}}_j^n$ as a convex combination of $\mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^n$, which leads to $\overline{\mathbf{U}}_j^n \in \Omega^{n} = \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1}$ due to the convexity of $\Omega$ (\Cref{lem:466}) and the hierarchy of global invariant domains (\Cref{lem:1889}). Additionally, all the cell-edge values of $\mathbf{U}^n_h$ belong to $\Omega^{n,1}$, since (i) For $j = 1,\dots,N_x$, $\mathbf{U}^n_h(x_{j-\frac12}^{+}) = \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,1}) \in \Omega^{n} = \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1}$, $\mathbf{U}^n_h(x_{j+\frac12}^{-}) = \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,L}) \in \Omega^{n} = \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1}$; (ii) By \Cref{lem:1872}, $\mathbf{U}^n_h(x_{\frac12}^{-}) \in \Omega^{n,1}$ and $\mathbf{U}^n_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,1}$. Therefore, we can apply \Cref{lem:2154} on $\mathbf{U}^n_h$ to obtain $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widetilde{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}$ for all $j$, and then \Cref{lem:1625b} to obtain $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}$ for all $j$. After applying the BP limiter to $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}^{n,1}_h$, \Cref{lem:1775} implies that the first RK stage is BP, namely, $\overline{\mathbf{U}}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}, \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_h(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,1}$ for all $j$ and $\ell$. Using similar arguments, we can prove the BP properties of the second and third RK stages: $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_h(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,s}$ for any $j$, $\ell$, and $s = 2,3$. Noticing that $\mathbf{U}^{n+1}_h = \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h$ and $\Omega^{n+1} = \Omega^{n,3}$, the claim \eqref{eq:2177} is proven.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Cell averages and edge values lie in $\Omega^{n,1}$; Lemma 4.5, Prop. 3.1 and Lemma 4.4 give BP for each RK stage.

nodes.name: Local BP property of BP-OEDG scheme
nodes.statement: If the local invariant domains $\Omega^{n,s}_j$ defined in \eqref{eq:1851} are considered, then the scheme \eqref{BPOE} with $\alpha \ge \max_j \alpha_{\max}(\mathbf{U}^-_{j+\frac12},\mathbf{U}^+_{j+\frac12})$ and under the CFL condition \eqref{eq:2300} is locally BP, namely, \begin{equation} \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n}_j ~~ \forall j ~ \forall \ell ~~ \Longrightarrow ~~ \mathbf{U}^{n+1}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n+1}_j ~~ \forall j ~ \forall \ell. \end{equation}
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: With local invariant domains, the BP-OEDG scheme keeps Gauss-Lobatto values in $\Omega^n_j$ under the CFL condition.
assumptions: the local invariant domains $\Omega^{n,s}_j$ defined in \eqref{eq:1851} are considered
with $\alpha \ge \max_j \alpha_{\max}(\mathbf{U}^-_{j+\frac12},\mathbf{U}^+_{j+\frac12})$ and under the CFL condition \eqref{eq:2300}
nodes.label: lem:2394

nodes.name: Local BP property (4.17)
nodes.statement: \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n}_j ~~ \forall j ~ \forall \ell ~~ \Longrightarrow ~~ \mathbf{U}^{n+1}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n+1}_j ~~ \forall j ~ \forall \ell.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.label: eq:2274

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 4.7
nodes.statement: Let us consider four cases: \begin{itemize}[leftmargin= 6mm] \item[(i)] If $j = 2,\dots,N_x$, then from \eqref{eq:1851}--\eqref{eq:1982}, we can obtain \begin{equation*} \left. \begin{aligned} && \mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-}) = \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j-1}(x^{\tt GL}_{j-1,L})\\ && \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j-1}(x^{\tt GL}_{j-1,L}) \in \Omega^{n, 0}_{j-1} \subseteq \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1} \\ && \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j-1}(x^{-}_{j-\frac12}) \in \Omega^{n, 0}_{j, *} \end{aligned} \right\} \; \Rightarrow \; \mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-}) \in \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n, 0}_{j, *} = \Omega^{n, 1}_{j}. \end{equation*} \item[(ii)] If $j = 1$, $\mathbf{U}^{n,0}_h(x_{\frac12}^{-}) \in \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{1,*} = \Omega^{n,1}_{1}$. \item[(iii)] If $j = 1,\dots,N_x-1$, then from \eqref{eq:1851}--\eqref{eq:1982}, we can obtain \begin{equation*} \left. \begin{aligned} && \mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+}) = \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j+1}(x^{\tt GL}_{j+1,1}) \\ && \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j+1}(x^{\tt GL}_{j+1,1}) \in \Omega^{n, 0}_{j+1} \subseteq \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1} \\ && \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j+1}(x^{+}_{j+\frac12}) \in \Omega^{n, 0}_{j, *} \end{aligned} \right\} \;\Rightarrow \; \mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n, 0}_{j, *} = \Omega^{n, 1}_{j}. \end{equation*} \item[(iv)] If $j = N_x$, $\mathbf{U}^{n,0}_h(x_{N_x +\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{N_x,*} = \Omega^{n,1}_{N_x}$. \end{itemize} To summarize, $\mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-}) \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ and $\mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for $j = 1,\dots,N_x$. On the other hand, \eqref{eq:1851}--\eqref{eq:1927} implies that $\mathbf{U}_h(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,0} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{j,*} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{j,*} = \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for all $j$. Therefore, we can use \Cref{lem:2154} to obtain $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widetilde{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for all $j$, and then \Cref{lem:1625b} to obtain $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for all $j$. Following this, we may apply \Cref{lem:1775} to conclude with the local BP property of the first RK stage, namely, $\mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for all $j$ and $\ell$. Via the similar arguments, we can prove the local BP properties of the second and the third RK stages: $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_h(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,s}$ for all $j$, $\ell$, and $s = 2,3$. Noticing $\mathbf{U}^{n+1}_h = \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h$ and $\Omega^{n+1} = \Omega^{n,3}$, the claim \eqref{eq:2274} is proven.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Case analysis on interior and boundary cells shows edge values lie in $\Omega_j^{n,1}$; then Lemma 4.5, Prop. 3.1 and Lemma 4.4 per stage.

nodes.name: Extension to other SSP time discretizations
nodes.statement: The global and local BP properties can be similarly proven for other high-order SSP (RK or multi-step) time discretizations that can be expressed as a convex combination of forward Euler steps.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes

nodes.name: Comparison schemes (nonBP-OEDG, BPDG, conventional DG)
nodes.statement: For comparison purposes, we consider four numerical schemes: \begin{itemize}[topsep=3pt,itemsep=0pt,parsep=1pt,leftmargin=3mm] \item {\bf BP-OEDG schemes}: the numerical schemes introduced in \Cref{sec:BP-OEDG}. If not specified, the local invariant domains defined in \Cref{sec:local} are adopted; \item {\bf nonBP-OEDG schemes}: the OEDG schemes without the BP limiter; \item {\bf BPDG schemes}: the DG schemes with BP limiter and without OE procedure; \item {\bf conventional DG schemes}: the DG schemes without the OE procedure and BP limiter. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Example 5.1: Smooth accuracy test with near-vacuum
nodes.statement: Consider the following smooth initial condition: \begin{equation*} \rho(x,0) = 0.05 \left(1 + \cos{\pi x} \right) + 10^{-8}, \quad v(x,0) \equiv 0.15, \quad c(x,0) \equiv 1, \end{equation*} with parameters \( v_{\rm ref} = 0.01 \), and \( \gamma \in \{0,1,2\} \). The computational domain is \([0,1]\) with periodic boundary conditions at both boundaries. The exact solution reads \begin{equation*} \rho(x, t) = 0.05 \Big[ 1 + \cos{(\pi (x - 0.15 \, t))} \Big] + 10^{-8}, \quad v(x, t) \equiv 0.15, \quad c(x,t) \equiv 1. \end{equation*} We compute the numerical solution up to \( t = 0.05 \) using the BP-OEDG scheme. The \( L_1 \) errors of the obtained numerical results are presented in Table \ref{Table1}, confirming the expected third-order accuracy. Please note that near-vacuum states appear in the solution. Employing nonBP-OEDG schemes for this example may produce numerical solutions with negative density, which can lead to simulation failure. For example, if the nonBP-OEDG method is used, the simulation would fail due to negative density in the numerical results; see \Cref{tab:2830} for the failure time. \begin{table}[th!] \caption{\sf Example \ref{exam1}, the $L_{1}$ errors in $\rho$ and the convergence rates for various $\gamma$ values.} \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{clclclc} \toprule[1.5pt] \multicolumn{1}{c}{\multirow{2} * {$N$}} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{ $\gamma = 0$} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{$\gamma = 1$} & \multicolumn{2}{c}{$\gamma = 2$} \\ \cmidrule(lr){2-3} \cmidrule(lr){4-5} \cmidrule(lr){6-7} \multicolumn{1}{c}{} &$L_1$ error & order & $L_1$ error & order & $L_1$ error & order \\ \midrule[1.5pt] 10 & 9.95e-6 & -- & 1.02e-4 & -- & 1.02e-4 & -- \\ 20 & 2.24e-6 & 2.15 & 1.73e-5 & 2.57 & 1.72e-5 & 2.57 \\ 40 & 4.64e-7 & 2.27 & 3.48e-7 & 5.63 & 3.48e-7 & 5.63 \\ 80 & 5.13e-8 & 3.18 & 4.68e-8 & 2.89 & 4.66e-8 & 2.90 \\ 160 & 7.70e-9 & 2.74 & 9.97e-9 & 2.23 & 5.54e-9 & 3.07 \\ 320 & 9.79e-10 & 2.97 & 5.65e-10 & 4.14 & 5.64e-10 & 3.30 \\ \bottomrule[1.5pt] \end{tabular} \end{center} \end{table} \begin{table}[th!] \caption{\sf Example \ref{exam1}, the time of simulation failure due to negative density in numerical results of the nonBP-OEDG scheme.} \begin{center} \begin{tabular}{cccc} \toprule[1.5pt] $N$ & $\gamma = 0$ & $\gamma = 1$ & $\gamma = 2$ \\ \midrule[1.5pt] 160 & $t \approx 2.17 \times 10^{-2}$ & $t \approx 1.81 \times 10^{-2}$ & $t \approx 1.51 \times 10^{-2}$ \\ 320 & $t \approx 1.74 \times 10^{-2}$ & $t \approx 9.03 \times 10^{-3}$ & $t \approx 9.08 \times 10^{-3}$ \\ \bottomrule[1.5pt] \end{tabular} \end{center} \end{table}

nodes.name: Example 5.2: Riemann problem: OE eliminates oscillations
nodes.statement: This example verifies the effectiveness and necessity of the OE procedure for eliminating oscillations. Consider the Riemann problem with initial data: \[ (\rho,v,c)(x,0) = \begin{dcases} (0.8,0.1,1) & {\rm if }~ x \le 0.5, \\ (0.5,0.2,1) & {\rm otherwise}, \end{dcases} \] with $\gamma = 2$. \Cref{oscillationFig} presents the numerical solutions at $t = 0.4$ obtained using BP-OEDG, BPDG, and conventional DG schemes. One can see that the BPDG and conventional DG schemes introduce spurious numerical oscillations, while the results of BP-OEDG scheme are free of oscillations. \begin{figure}[t!] \begin{center} \includegraphics[width = 0.49\textwidth,trim=25 15 35 15,clip]{./0611/125rho_oscillation.pdf} \includegraphics[width = 0.49\textwidth,trim=25 15 35 15,clip]{./0611/125v_oscillation.pdf} \caption{\sf Example \ref{exam2}, the numerical results of density and velocity obtained by using the BP-OEDG, BPDG, and conventional DG schemes, $t = 0.4$, $\Delta x = 1/300$.} \end{center} \end{figure}

nodes.name: Example 5.4: Global vs local invariant domains
nodes.statement: In this example, we compare the BP-OEDG scheme with global (\Cref{sec:global}) and local invariant domains (\Cref{sec:local}). Consider the following initial condition: \[ (\rho,v,c)(x,0) = \begin{dcases} (1\times 10^{-12},10,1) & {\rm if } ~ x < 0.25, \\ (0.8,0.5,1) & {\rm if } ~ 0.25 \le x < 0.985, \\ (0.5,400,1) & {\rm if } ~ x \ge 0.985. \end{dcases} \] The parameter $\gamma = 0$. The numerical results obtained by the locally and globally BP-OEDG schemes are shown in \Cref{fig:LG}. As one can see, even with a global constraint $w \le w_{\max}$ enforced, a non-physical velocity overshoot can still be observed in the numerical results obtained by the globally BP-OEDG scheme. This is due to the global $w$ upper bound ($\approx$ 399.37) being much larger than the local $w$ upper bound ($\approx$ 0.30) near $x = 0.25$. In this case, enforcing a global constraint $w \le w_{\max}$ can no longer help mitigate the $v$-overshoot in the vicinity. \begin{figure}[th!] \centerline{ \hfill \begin{subfigure}[t][][t]{0.47\textwidth} \includegraphics[trim=25 15 41 15,clip,width=\textwidth]{./0611/333LBPGBP.pdf} \caption{\sf linear scale} \end{subfigure} \hfill \begin{subfigure}[t][][t]{0.47\textwidth} \includegraphics[trim=25 15 41 15,clip,width=\textwidth]{./0611/333LBPGBPs.pdf} \caption{\sf logarithmic scale} \end{subfigure} \hfill } \caption{\sf Example \ref{exam_LG}, BP-OEDG scheme with global and local invariant domains, $t =0.0305$, $\Delta x = 1/300$.} \end{figure}
