nodes.name: Road network discretization
nodes.statement: Consider a road network consists of $N_R$ road segments and $N_J$ junctions, we partition the spatial domain on the $r$-th road by $N_x^{(r)}$ uniform cells $\big\{I_j^{(r)} := [x^{(r)}_{j - \frac{1}{2}}, x^{(r)}_{j + \frac{1}{2}}] \big \}_{j = 1}^{N_x^{(r)}}$.

nodes.name: Incoming/outgoing road index sets
nodes.statement: Let $\delta_{\ell}^-$ (resp. $\delta_{\ell}^+$) denote the set of indices representing incoming (resp. outgoing) roads connected to the Junction $\ell$.

nodes.name: Coupling condition at junctions
nodes.statement: Given the traffic states in the vicinity of the junction, namely, \[ \textrm{the input of coupling condition:} \quad \left \{ \mathbf{U}^{(i)}_h \left(x_{N_x^{(i)} + \frac{1}{2}}^{(i), -} \right) \right \}_{i \in \delta_\ell^-} {\rm and} \quad \bigg\{ \mathbf{U}^{(j)}_h \bigg(x_{\frac{1}{2}}^{(j), +} \bigg) \bigg\}_{j \in \delta_\ell^+}, \] a coupling condition should be employed to determine the corresponding traffic states immediately outside the computational domain, that is, \[ \textrm{the output of coupling condition:} \quad \left \{ \mathbf{U}^{(i)}_h \left(x_{N_x^{(i)} + \frac{1}{2}}^{(i), +} \right) \right \}_{i \in \delta_\ell^-} {\rm and} \quad \bigg\{ \mathbf{U}^{(j)}_h \bigg(x_{\frac{1}{2}}^{(j), -} \bigg) \bigg\}_{j \in \delta_\ell^+}, \] which are required to evolve the numerical solutions $\{\mathbf{U}^{(r)}_h\}_{r=1}^{N_r}$ to the next time step, and are also used in updating global invariant domains (see \eqref{eq:1807}) and local invariant domains (see \eqref{eq:1917}--\eqref{eq:1982}).
nodes.statement_short: A coupling condition maps traffic states near a junction to the ghost states outside each road's domain.

nodes.name: HB and GHMW network settings
nodes.statement: In order to validate the robustness of the proposed BP-OEDG schemes on road network applications, we consider two different settings in the following numerical experiments: \begin{itemize}[leftmargin=9mm] \item{\bf HB network}: The original ARZ model with the coupling condition from \cite{haut2007second} on networks with diverging and/or merging junctions. \item{\bf GHMW network}: The AP ARZ model with the coupling condition from \cite{gottlich2021second} on networks with diverging, merging, and/or hybrid junctions. \end{itemize}

nodes.name: Junction traffic fluxes q_ji
nodes.statement: For $j \in \delta_\ell^+$ and $i \in \delta_\ell^-$, $q_{ji} \geq 0$ denotes the traffic flux from Road $i$ to Road $j$, and we denote by $q_i^{-}$ (resp. $q_j^+$) the total incoming (resp. outgoing) flux of Road $i$ (resp. $j$), namely, $q_i^- = \sum_{j \in \delta_\ell^+} q_{ji}$, $q_j^+ = \sum_{i \in \delta_\ell^-} q_{ji}$.

nodes.name: Traffic distribution matrix
nodes.statement: For a junction with multiple incoming and outgoing roads, one should specify a traffic distribution matrix $\mathcal{A} = (a_{ji})_{i \in \delta_\ell^-, j \in \delta_\ell^+}$, where $0 \leq a_{ji} \leq 1$, and $q_{ji} = a_{ji} q_i^-$.

nodes.name: Priority vector beta
nodes.statement: For the GHMW network, the fluxes $\mathbf{q}_j = (q_{ji})_{i \in \delta_\ell^-}$ of an outgoing Road $j$, are proportional to a given vector $\boldsymbol{\beta} = (\beta_i)_{i \in \delta_\ell^-}$.

nodes.name: Example 5.5: Diverging junction, AP ARZ
nodes.statement: In this example, we use the AP ARZ model ($\gamma = 1$) to simulate traffic flows near a diverging junction with one incoming road (Road 1) and two outgoing roads (Roads 2 and 3). The initial conditions on these roads are given by \begin{equation*} \begin{gathered} \rho^{(1)}(x,0) = \rho^{(3)}(x,0) = 0.1, \quad \rho^{(2)}(x,0) = \left\{ \begin{aligned} & 0.2, \; &&{\rm if} \; x \in [0.2, 0.4] \cup [0.6, 0.8],\\ & 0.1, \; &&{\rm otherwise}, \end{aligned}\right. \\ w^{(r)}(x,0) = c^{(r)}(x,0) = 1, \; r = 1, 2, 3. \end{gathered} \end{equation*} The traffic flow entering the junction from incoming Road 1 is equally distributed between outgoing Roads 2 and 3. We implement the proposed BP-OEDG scheme to solve this problem, and the obtained numerical results, presented in \Cref{fig:T4}, align consistently with the results presented in \cite{buli2020discontinuous} and \cite{canic2015runge}. \begin{figure}[h!] \centering \centerline{ \includegraphics[trim=25 55 41 75,clip,width = 0.5\textwidth]{./Diverging/25rho.pdf} \includegraphics[trim=25 55 41 75,clip,width = 0.5\textwidth]{./Diverging/25v.pdf} } \caption{\sf Example \ref{exam3a}, BP-OEDG scheme, $t = 0.25$, $\Delta x = 1/300$. Reference solutions are depicted in black dashed lines.} \end{figure}
nodes.label: exam3a

nodes.name: Example 5.6: HB diverging junction with three outgoing roads
nodes.statement: We consider an HB network consisting of one diverging junction, one incoming road (Road 1) and three outgoing roads (Roads 2--4). The initial conditions on these roads are given by \begin{gather*} \rho^{(1)}(x,0) = \rho^{(3)}(x,0) = 0.1, \quad \rho^{(2)}(x,0) = \begin{dcases} 10^{-10} & {\rm if} \; x \in [0.2, 0.4] \cup [0.6, 0.8], \\ 0.1 & {\rm otherwise}, \end{dcases} \\ \rho^{(4)}(x,0) = 0.05 \big[1 + \sin{(5 \pi x)}\big] + 10^{-10}, \quad w^{(r)}(x,0) = 0.5,\; r = 1, 2, 3, 4. \end{gather*} The traffic flow entering the junction from incoming Road 1 is equally distributed among outgoing Roads 2--4. The BP-OEDG scheme is used to solve this problem with $\gamma = 0$ and $\gamma = 2$, respectively. The obtained numerical results are presented in \Cref{fig:T5}. As one can see, the wave structures are sharply resolved, and they match well with the results reported in \cite{buli2020discontinuous,canic2015runge}. \begin{figure}[th!] \centering \centerline{ \includegraphics[trim=75 40 61 50,clip,width = 0.5\textwidth]{./Diverging/21rho.pdf} \includegraphics[trim=75 40 51 50,clip,width = 0.5\textwidth]{./Diverging/26rho.pdf} } \caption{\sf Example \ref{exam3b}, BP-OEDG scheme, $t = 0.1$, $\Delta x = 1/150$. Left: $\gamma = 0$; Right: $\gamma = 2$. Reference solutions are depicted in black dashed lines.} \end{figure}
nodes.label: exam3b

nodes.name: Example 5.7: HB vs GHMW junction conditions
nodes.statement: In this example, we compare the HB and GHMW junction conditions. We consider a diverging junction connected to one outgoing road (Road 1) and two incoming roads (Road 2--3). The initial conditions on these roads are given by $(\rho^{(1)},\rho^{(2)},\rho^{(3)})(x,0) = (2,4,6)$ and $(y^{(1)},y^{(2)},y^{(3)})(x,0) = (12,24,72)$. With respect to the GHMW networking setting, the priority vector is $\boldsymbol{\beta} = (1/2,1/2)^\top$. For HB network setting, please note that the priority vector $\boldsymbol{\beta}$ is determined by the traffic demands on the incoming roads. The BP-OEDG scheme is adopted to solve these problems, and the obtained numerical results are presented in \Cref{fig:T7}. As one can see, the discontinuities on Roads 2 and 3 are all well resolved without oscillations, while the contact discontinuities on Road 1 are slightly smeared. In \Cref{fig:T7b}, the discontinuity in $c$ is resolved without overshoots or undershoots, demonstrating that the proposed BP-OEDG method preserves the minimum and maximum principles of $c$. \begin{figure}[th!] \centering \begin{subfigure}[t][][t]{0.32\textwidth} \includegraphics[trim=25 45 55 82,clip,width = \textwidth]{./Merging/51_1_rho.pdf} \caption{\sf HB network, $c \equiv 1$.} \end{subfigure} \begin{subfigure}[t][][t]{0.64\textwidth} \includegraphics[trim=25 45 55 82,clip,width = 0.48\textwidth]{./Merging/51_2_rho.pdf} \includegraphics[trim=25 45 55 82,clip,width = 0.48\textwidth]{./20240427/51_2_c.pdf} \caption{\sf GHMW network.} \end{subfigure} \caption{\sf Example \ref{ex:T7}, BP-OEDG scheme, $t = 0.1$, $\gamma = 2$. Reference solutions are depicted in black dashed lines.} \end{figure}
nodes.label: ex:T7

nodes.name: Example 5.8: Merging junction with three incoming roads
nodes.statement: In this example, we consider a diverging junction which is connected to one outgoing road (Road 1) and three incoming roads (Road 2--4). All four road segments have length of 1. The initial conditions on these roads are given by \begin{gather*} \rho_0^{(1)}(x) = 0.02, \quad \rho_0^{(2)}(x) = \rho_0^{(3)}(x) = \rho_0^{(4)}(x) = \begin{dcases} 0.005 & {\rm if} \; x \in [0, 0.1],\\ 0.01 & {\rm if} \; x \in (0.1, 0.4] \cup (0.7, 1],\\ 0.02 & {\rm otherwise}. \end{dcases} \\ w^{(r)}(x,0) \equiv 0, \; r = 1, 2, 3, 4. \end{gather*} The HB junction condition is adopted. Specifically, all three incoming roads contribute identical traffic influx into the outgoing Road 1. The BP-OEDG scheme is used to solve this problem, and the obtained numerical results are demonstrated in \Cref{fig:T6}. \begin{figure}[h!] \centering \centerline{ \includegraphics[trim=55 30 61 30,clip,width = 0.5\textwidth]{./Merging/31rho.pdf} \includegraphics[trim=55 30 61 30,clip,width = 0.5\textwidth]{./Merging/31v.pdf} } \caption{\sf Example \ref{ex:T6}, $\gamma = 0$, BP-OEDG scheme, $t = 0.08$, $\Delta x = 1/150$. Reference solutions are depicted in black dashed lines.} \end{figure}
nodes.label: ex:T6

nodes.name: Example 5.9: Seven-road three-junction network
nodes.statement: In this example, we test the propose BP-OEDG scheme on a traffic simulation over a network involving seven roads and three junctions, as depicted in \Cref{fig:T8}. The initial conditions are given by \begin{align*} & \rho^{(1)}(x,0) = \rho^{(2)}(x,0) = \rho^{(6)}(x,0) = 0.1, \quad \rho^{(7)}(x,0) = 10^{-10}, \\ & \rho^{(3)}(x,0) = \rho^{(5)}(x,0) = \begin{dcases} 0.18 + 10^{-10} & {\rm if} \; x \in [0, 0.1], \\ 0.1 \left[ 0.9 + (1-x) \cos\left(\frac{25 \pi (x - 0.1)}{0.9}\right)\right] + 10^{-10} & {\rm otherwise}, \end{dcases} \\ & \rho^{(4)}(x,0) = 0.1 \big[1 + x \cos{(25 \pi x}) \big] + 10^{-10}, \quad w_0^{(r)}(x) = 0.5, \; r = 1, \cdots, 7. \end{align*} The parameter $\gamma = 2$. At Junction A, the traffic distribution matrix is given by \( \mathcal{A} = \begin{pmatrix} 0.5 & 0.5 \\ 0.5 & 0.5 \end{pmatrix} \), and both Junctions A and B have the priority vector $\boldsymbol{\beta} = (0.5,0.5)^\top$. At Junction C, incoming traffic flux is evenly distributed between outgoing Roads 4 and 7. The proposed BP-OEDG scheme is used to conduct the simulation, and the results are presented in \Cref{fig:T8}. The trigonometric traffic waves initially located on Roads 3, 4, and 5, are accurately presented by the numerical results on a relatively coarse mesh. The discontinuity initially located on Road 4 passes through Junction A, and then introduces discontinuities on Roads 1 and 3, both of which are sharply resolved without oscillations. On Road 7, a discontinuity with near-vacuum state on its downstream side is captured without noticeable overshoots or undershoots. \begin{figure}[th!] \centering \includegraphics[trim=0 55 0 110,clip,width = 0.7\textwidth]{./Complex/46rho.pdf} \caption{\sf Example \ref{ex:T8}, BP-OEDG scheme, $\Delta x = 1/150$, $t = 0.25$. Reference solutions are depicted in black dashed lines.} \end{figure}
nodes.label: ex:T8

nodes.name: Example 5.10: 48-road 25-junction network
nodes.statement: In the last example, we consider a network with 48 roads and 25 junctions. In \Cref{fig:T9a}, a schematic diagram of the network is shown, and each road segment is assigned a color: black, blue, red or green. The initial conditions on these roads are given according to the color assigned: \begin{align*} & \rho^{\text{black}}(x,0) \equiv 10^{-10}, \quad \rho^{\text{blue}}(x,0) \equiv 0.1, \quad \rho^{\text{red}}(x,0) = 0.1 \left[ 1 + x \cos{(25 \pi x})\right] + 10^{-10}, \\ & \rho^{\text{green}}(x,0) = \begin{dcases} 0.1 & {\rm if} \; x \in [0.1, 0.9], \\ 10^{-10} & {\rm otherwise}, \end{dcases} \quad w^{(\cdot)}(x,0) \equiv 0.5 \quad \textrm{for all road segments}. \end{align*} The parameter $\gamma = 1$ and the HB junction condition is adopted. The proposed BP-OEDG scheme is adopted to simulate this test, and the resulting numerical solution on Roads 1, 26, and 44 are shown in \Cref{fig:T9b}. \begin{figure}[h!] \centering \includegraphics[trim=185 25 162 18,clip,width = 0.5\textwidth]{./Complex/complexRd.pdf} \caption{\sf Example \ref{ex:T9}, schematic diagram of the network.} \end{figure} \begin{figure}[h!] \centering \centerline{ \begin{subfigure}[t][][t]{0.32\textwidth} \includegraphics[trim=25 15 35 15,clip,width = \textwidth]{./Complex/47rho1.pdf} \caption{\sf Road 1.} \end{subfigure} \begin{subfigure}[t][][t]{0.32\textwidth} \includegraphics[trim=25 15 35 15,clip,width = \textwidth]{./Complex/47rho2.pdf} \caption{\sf Road 26.} \end{subfigure} \begin{subfigure}[t][][t]{0.32\textwidth} \includegraphics[trim=25 15 35 15,clip,width = \textwidth]{./Complex/47rho3.pdf} \caption{\sf Road 44.} \end{subfigure} } \caption{\sf \Cref{ex:T9}, BP-OEDG scheme, $t = 0.25$, $\Delta x = 1/150$. Reference solutions are depicted in black dashed lines.} \end{figure}
nodes.label: ex:T9

nodes.name: Part I: Omega_0 convex
nodes.statement: {\sf Part I}: The set $\Omega_0$ is clearly convex.
nodes.statement_short: $\Omega_0$ is convex.

nodes.name: Part II: Omega_1 convex
nodes.statement: {\sf Part II}: For any two states $\mathbf{U}_0 = (\rho_0,y_0,z_0)^\top$ and $\mathbf{U}_1 = (\rho_1,y_1,z_1)^\top \in \Omega_1$, and any $\theta \in [0,1]$, let us denote $ (\rho_\theta, y_\theta, z_\theta)^\top = (1 - \theta) \mathbf{U}_0 + \theta \mathbf{U}_1$. In the following, we will prove that $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_1$. First, the positivity of $\rho_\theta$ can be obtained by $\rho_\theta = (1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1 \ge \min\{\rho_1,\rho_0\} > 0$. Since \begin{align*} w_\theta = \frac{y_\theta}{\rho_\theta} = \frac {(1 - \theta) y_0 + \theta y_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} & = \left( \frac{(1 - \theta) \rho_0}{(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) w_0 + \left( \frac {\theta \rho_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) w_1, \\ c_\theta = \frac{z_\theta}{\rho_\theta} = \frac {(1 - \theta) z_0 + \theta z_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} & = \left( \frac{(1 - \theta) \rho_0}{(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) c_0 + \left( \frac {\theta \rho_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) c_1, \end{align*} namely, $w_\theta$ (resp. $c_\theta$) is a convex combination of $w_0$ and $w_1$ (resp. $c_0$ and $c_1$), we have $w_\theta \in [w_{\min},w_{\max}]$ (resp. $c_\theta \in [c_{\min},c_{\max}]$). Thus, $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_1$ and $\Omega_1$ is convex.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\Omega_1$ convex via convex-combination formulas for $w$, $c$.

nodes.name: Introduce convex combination
nodes.statement: For any two states $\mathbf{U}_0 = (\rho_0,y_0,z_0)^\top$ and $\mathbf{U}_1 = (\rho_1,y_1,z_1)^\top \in \Omega_1$, and any $\theta \in [0,1]$, let us denote $ (\rho_\theta, y_\theta, z_\theta)^\top = (1 - \theta) \mathbf{U}_0 + \theta \mathbf{U}_1$. In the following, we will prove that $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Introduce $U_\theta$ as a convex combination of two states.

nodes.name: Positivity of rho_theta
nodes.statement: First, the positivity of $\rho_\theta$ can be obtained by $\rho_\theta = (1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1 \ge \min\{\rho_1,\rho_0\} > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: $\rho_\theta>0$.

nodes.name: w and c bounds
nodes.statement: Since \begin{align*} w_\theta = \frac{y_\theta}{\rho_\theta} = \frac {(1 - \theta) y_0 + \theta y_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} & = \left( \frac{(1 - \theta) \rho_0}{(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) w_0 + \left( \frac {\theta \rho_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) w_1, \\ c_\theta = \frac{z_\theta}{\rho_\theta} = \frac {(1 - \theta) z_0 + \theta z_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} & = \left( \frac{(1 - \theta) \rho_0}{(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) c_0 + \left( \frac {\theta \rho_1} {(1 - \theta) \rho_0 + \theta \rho_1} \right) c_1, \end{align*} namely, $w_\theta$ (resp. $c_\theta$) is a convex combination of $w_0$ and $w_1$ (resp. $c_0$ and $c_1$), we have $w_\theta \in [w_{\min},w_{\max}]$ (resp. $c_\theta \in [c_{\min},c_{\max}]$). Thus, $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_1$ and $\Omega_1$ is convex.
nodes.statement_short: $w_\theta$, $c_\theta$ are convex combinations, so they keep their bounds.

nodes.name: Part III: Omega_2 convex
nodes.statement: {\sf Part III}: Now, let us assume $\mathbf{U}_0$ and $\mathbf{U}_1 \in \Omega_2$. The positivity of $z_\theta$ can be obtained by $z_\theta = (1 - \theta) z_0 + \theta z_1 \ge \min\{z_1,z_0\} > 0$. Additionally, we need to show $v_\theta \ge v_{\min}$. Consider a function of $\rho$ and $z$ defined as \begin{equation} \eta(\rho,z) := \rho (v_{\min} + p(\rho, z)) = y+\rho(v_{\min}-v) , \end{equation} such that for state $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,y,z)^\top$, the condition $v(\mathbf{U}) \ge v_{\min}$ is equivalent to $y \ge \eta(\rho,z)$. Since $y_\theta \ge \eta(\rho_\theta,z_\theta)$ for $\theta = 0$ and $1$, in order to prove $v_\theta \ge v_{\min}$, or equivalently, $y_\theta \ge \eta(\rho_\theta,z_\theta)$, we only need to show that the function $\eta(\rho,z)$ is convex for $(\rho,z) \in \mathbb{R}_+ \times \mathbb{R}_+$. To this end, we will show that its Hessian matrix $\mathbf{H}$ is positive semi-definite. In the case of $\gamma = 0$, the Hessian matrix is given by \( \mathbf{H} = {\rm diag}\{ v_{\rm ref}/\rho, 0 \}, \) which is clearly positive semi-definite. In the case of $\gamma > 0$, \[ \mathbf{H} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} \left(\begin{array}{cc} (\kappa-\gamma)(\kappa-\gamma-1) z^2 & -\kappa(\kappa-\gamma-1)z\rho \\ -\kappa(\kappa-\gamma-1)z\rho & \kappa (\kappa-1) \rho^2 \end{array}\right), \] and the determinants of its principle minors are given by \begin{gather*} \mathbf{H}_{11} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa+2}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} (\kappa-\gamma)(\kappa-\gamma-1) \ge 0, \quad \mathbf{H}_{22} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa+1} \kappa (\kappa-1) \ge 0, \\ |\mathbf{H}| = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa+2}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} \left[ (\gamma-\kappa)(\gamma-\kappa+1) \kappa(\kappa-1)-\kappa^2(\gamma-\kappa+1)^2 \right] \ge 0. \end{gather*} Thus, we conclude that $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_2$ and $\Omega_2$ is convex.
nodes.statement_short: Show $\Omega_2$ convex by convexity of $\eta$.

nodes.name: Positivity of z_theta
nodes.statement: Now, let us assume $\mathbf{U}_0$ and $\mathbf{U}_1 \in \Omega_2$. The positivity of $z_\theta$ can be obtained by $z_\theta = (1 - \theta) z_0 + \theta z_1 \ge \min\{z_1,z_0\} > 0$.
nodes.statement_short: $z_\theta>0$.

nodes.name: Introduce eta
nodes.statement: Additionally, we need to show $v_\theta \ge v_{\min}$. Consider a function of $\rho$ and $z$ defined as \begin{equation} \eta(\rho,z) := \rho (v_{\min} + p(\rho, z)) = y+\rho(v_{\min}-v) , \end{equation} such that for state $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,y,z)^\top$, the condition $v(\mathbf{U}) \ge v_{\min}$ is equivalent to $y \ge \eta(\rho,z)$.
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite $v\ge v_{min}$ as $y\ge\eta(\rho,z)$.

nodes.name: Reduce to convexity of eta
nodes.statement: Since $y_\theta \ge \eta(\rho_\theta,z_\theta)$ for $\theta = 0$ and $1$, in order to prove $v_\theta \ge v_{\min}$, or equivalently, $y_\theta \ge \eta(\rho_\theta,z_\theta)$, we only need to show that the function $\eta(\rho,z)$ is convex for $(\rho,z) \in \mathbb{R}_+ \times \mathbb{R}_+$. To this end, we will show that its Hessian matrix $\mathbf{H}$ is positive semi-definite.
nodes.statement_short: Suffices that $\eta$ is convex, i.e. its Hessian is PSD.

nodes.name: Case gamma = 0
nodes.statement: In the case of $\gamma = 0$, the Hessian matrix is given by \( \mathbf{H} = {\rm diag}\{ v_{\rm ref}/\rho, 0 \}, \) which is clearly positive semi-definite.
nodes.statement_short: Hessian diagonal and PSD.

nodes.name: Case gamma > 0
nodes.statement: In the case of $\gamma > 0$, \[ \mathbf{H} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} \left(\begin{array}{cc} (\kappa-\gamma)(\kappa-\gamma-1) z^2 & -\kappa(\kappa-\gamma-1)z\rho \\ -\kappa(\kappa-\gamma-1)z\rho & \kappa (\kappa-1) \rho^2 \end{array}\right), \] and the determinants of its principle minors are given by \begin{gather*} \mathbf{H}_{11} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa+2}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} (\kappa-\gamma)(\kappa-\gamma-1) \ge 0, \quad \mathbf{H}_{22} = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa+1} \kappa (\kappa-1) \ge 0, \\ |\mathbf{H}| = \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma}z^{\kappa+2}\rho^{\gamma-\kappa-1} \left[ (\gamma-\kappa)(\gamma-\kappa+1) \kappa(\kappa-1)-\kappa^2(\gamma-\kappa+1)^2 \right] \ge 0. \end{gather*}
nodes.statement_short: Principal minors of the Hessian are nonnegative.

nodes.name: Omega_2 convex
nodes.statement: Thus, we conclude that $\mathbf{U}_\theta \in \Omega_2$ and $\Omega_2$ is convex.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude $\Omega_2$ convex.

nodes.name: Part IV: Omega convex
nodes.statement: {\sf Part IV}: Since both $\Omega_1$ and $\Omega_2$ are convex, their intersection $\Omega$ is also convex.
nodes.statement_short: Intersection of convex sets is convex.

nodes.name: Derivative of h in z_*
nodes.statement: Note that \[ h_{z_*}(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) = \rho_*\left[ \left(\rho_*-\rho\right) p_{\rho z}(\rho_*, z_*) + (z_*-z) p_{zz}(\rho_*, z_*) + p_z(\rho_*, z_*) \right] -\rho p_z(\rho_*, z_*) \]
nodes.statement_short: Compute $h_{z_*}$.

nodes.name: Case gamma > 0: sign of h_{z*}
nodes.statement: We first consider the case of $\gamma > 0$. In this case, \[ h_{z_*}(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) = \frac{\kappa v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma} z_*^{\kappa-2} \rho_*^{\gamma-\kappa} \Big[ \gamma \rho_*z_* + (\kappa-\gamma-1) \rho z_* - (\kappa-1) \rho_* z \Big], \] which, due to $\kappa \ge \gamma+1$ and the positivities of $\rho_*$, $z_*$, $\rho$, and $z$, implies that \[ \begin{dcases} h_{z_*}(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) \ge 0 & {\rm if} ~ z_* \ge \frac{(\kappa-1) \rho_* z}{\gamma \rho_* + (\kappa-\gamma-1) \rho} =: z_\star, \\ h_{z_*}(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) < 0 & {\rm otherwise}. \end{dcases} \]
nodes.statement_short: For $\gamma>0$, $h_{z_*}$ changes sign at $z_\star$.

nodes.name: Minimize over z_*
nodes.statement: Therefore, \begin{align*} h(\rho_*, z_*;\rho,z) \ge h\left(\rho_*, z_\star;\rho,z\right) = \rho p (\rho, z) - \frac{v_{\rm ref}}{\gamma} z \, \rho_*^{\gamma - \kappa + 1} z_\star^{\kappa - 1} =: \tilde{h}(\rho_*;\rho,z). \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $h\ge\tilde h(\rho_*;\rho,z)$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity in rho_*
nodes.statement: Taking partial derivative of $\tilde{h}(\rho_*;\rho,z)$ with respect to $\rho_*$ gives \[ \tilde h_{\rho_*}(\rho_*;\rho,z) = v_{\rm ref} \frac{\kappa - \gamma - 1}{\kappa - 1} (\rho_* -\rho) \, \rho_* ^{\gamma -\kappa -1} z_\star^\kappa, \] which implies $\tilde h(\rho_*;\rho,z)$ is increasing with respect to $\rho_*$ if $\rho_* \ge \rho$, and decreasing if $\rho_* < \rho$.
nodes.statement_short: $\tilde h$ decreases then increases in $\rho_*$ around $\rho$.

nodes.name: Conclude gamma > 0
nodes.statement: Therefore, $\tilde h(\rho_*;\rho,z) \ge \tilde h(\rho;\rho,z)$, and we finally have \[ h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \ge \tilde h(\rho_*;\rho,z) \ge \tilde h(\rho;\rho,z) = h(\rho,z;\rho,z) = 0. \]
nodes.statement_short: Chain the bounds to get $h\ge0$.

nodes.name: Case gamma = 0
nodes.statement: In the remaining case of $\gamma = 0$, $p(\rho,z) = v_{\rm ref} \log \rho$, and \[ h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) = v_{\rm ref} \left( \rho \log \rho - \rho \log \rho_* + \rho_* - \rho \right) =: \hat{h}(\rho_*;\rho). \]
nodes.statement_short: For $\gamma=0$, $h$ reduces to $\hat h(\rho_*;\rho)$.

nodes.name: Monotonicity of hat h
nodes.statement: Taking derivative with respect to $\rho_*$ yields $\hat{h}_{\rho_*}(\rho_*;\rho)=v_{\rm ref}(\rho_*-\rho)/\rho_*$, indicating $\hat{h}(\rho_*;\rho)$ is increasing with respect to $\rho_*$ if $\rho_* \ge \rho$, and decreasing if $\rho_* < \rho$.
nodes.statement_short: $\hat h$ is minimized at $\rho_*=\rho$.

nodes.name: Conclude gamma = 0
nodes.statement: Therefore, in the case of $\gamma = 0$, we conclude the proof by \[ h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \ge \hat{h}(\rho_*;\rho) \ge \hat{h}(\rho;\rho) = h(\rho,z;\rho,z) = 0. \]
nodes.statement_short: $h\ge0$ for $\gamma=0$.

nodes.name: Bounds of split states
nodes.statement: Let $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm = (\hat{\rho}_\pm,\hat{y}_\pm,\hat{z}_\pm)^\top$, $\hat{v}_\pm = v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm)$, $\hat{w}_\pm = w(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm)$, and $\hat{c}_\pm = c(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm)$. Because $\alpha > v(\mathbf{U}) > 0$, we have $\hat{\rho}_\pm = \left( 1 \pm v(\mathbf{U})/\alpha \right) \rho > 0$, and \begin{equation*} \begin{aligned} \hat{w}_\pm - w_{\min} & = {(\hat{y}_\pm - \hat{\rho}_\pm \, w_{\min})}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} = \left( 1 \pm {v(\mathbf{U})}/{\alpha} \right) \left( {\rho}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm}\right) (w - w_{\min}) \geq 0, \\ w_{\max} - \hat{w}_\pm & = {(\hat{\rho}_\pm \, w_{\max} - \hat{y}_\pm)}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} = \left( 1 \pm {v(\mathbf{U})}/{\alpha} \right) \left( {\rho}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} \right) (w_{\max} - w) \geq 0, \\ \hat{c}_\pm - c_{\min} & = {(\hat{z}_\pm - \hat{\rho}_\pm \, c_{\min})}{\hat{\rho}_\pm} = \left( 1 \pm {v(\mathbf{U})}/{\alpha} \right) \left( {\rho}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} \right) (c - c_{\min}) \geq 0, \\ c_{\max} - \hat{c}_\pm & = {(\hat{\rho}_\pm \, c_{\max} - \hat{z}_\pm)}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} = \left( 1 \pm {v(\mathbf{U})}/{\alpha} \right) \left( {\rho}/{\hat{\rho}_\pm} \right) (c_{\max} - c) \geq 0. \end{aligned} \end{equation*}
nodes.statement_short: Positivity of $\hat\rho_\pm$ and bound gaps of $\hat w_\pm,\hat c_\pm$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: In summary, $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_\pm \in \Omega_1$. The proof is completed.
nodes.statement_short: $\widehat U_\pm\in\Omega_1$.

nodes.name: Omega_2 subset Omega_2^*
nodes.statement: On one hand, if $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,y,z)^\top \in \Omega_2$, then, $\rho > 0$, $z > 0$. Notice that, for any $\rho_* > 0$ and $z_* > 0$, \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* &= y - \rho \big( v_{\min} + p(\rho,z)\big) + h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \\ &\stackrel{\rm \Cref{lem:791}}{\ge} y - \rho \big( v_{\min} + p(\rho,z)\big) = \rho \big( v(\mathbf{U}) - v_{\min}\big) \ge 0 , \end{aligned} \end{equation} which implies that $\mathbf{U} \in \Omega_2^*$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 2.2 to show $U\in\Omega_2^*$.

nodes.name: Omega_2^* subset Omega_2
nodes.statement: On the other hand, if $\mathbf{U} \in \Omega_2^*$, then $\rho > 0$, $z > 0$. Notice that $\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* \ge 0$ for any $\rho_* > 0$ and $z_* > 0$. Taking $\rho_* = \rho$ and $z_* = z$ implies \[ \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}(\rho,z) + s(\rho,z) = y - \rho \big( v_{\min} + p(\rho,z)\big) = \rho \big( v(\mathbf{U}) - v_{\min}\big) \ge 0. \]
nodes.statement_short: Take $\rho_*=\rho$, $z_*=z$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, it holds that $\mathbf{U} \in \Omega_2$. The proof is completed.
nodes.statement_short: $U\in\Omega_2$.

nodes.name: Flux bound
nodes.statement: For any $\mathbf{U} = (\rho,y,z)^\top \in \Omega_2^*$, we denote $v = v(\mathbf{U}) \ge v_{\min}$, then \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} & ~~~ \pm \mathbf{F}(\mathbf{U}) \cdot \mathbf{n}_* \pm v_{\min} s_* \\ & = \pm v \, (\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) \pm (v_{\min}-v) s_* \le |v|\,(\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) +\frac{s_*}{\rho}\Big[ \rho (v-v_{\min}) \Big] \\ & \stackrel{\eqref{eq:632}}{\le} \, |v|\,(\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) + \frac{s_*}{\rho}(\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) = \left( |v|+\frac{s_*}{\rho} \right) (\mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) , \end{aligned} \end{equation} where the last inequality is due to \begin{equation} \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* = \rho (v-v_{\min}) + h(\rho_*,z_*;\rho,z) \stackrel{\rm \Cref{lem:791}}{\ge} \rho (v-v_{\min}). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\pm F\cdot n_*\pm v_{min}s_*$ by $(|v|+s_*/\rho)(U\cdot n_*+s_*)$.

nodes.name: Decompose GLF state
nodes.statement: Let us denote $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{v}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{v}}$} } v = v(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U})$, $\widehat{\mathbf{F}} = \mathbf{F}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})$, and $\widecheck{\mathbf{F}} = \mathbf{F}(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})$, then it implies \begin{equation} \begin{aligned} 2\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + 2s_* & = \left[~ \widehat{\mathbf{U}} + \alpha^{-1} \widehat{\mathbf{F}} + \widecheck{\mathbf{U}} - \alpha^{-1} \widecheck{\mathbf{F}} ~\right] \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + 2 s_* \\ & = \widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + \widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + \alpha^{-1} \left( \widehat{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* - \widecheck{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + v_{\min} s_* - v_{\min} s_* \right) + 2 s_* \\ & = \widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + \widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + 2s_* - \alpha^{-1} \left( \widecheck{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + v_{\min} s_* \right) - \alpha^{-1} \left(-\widehat{\mathbf{F}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* - v_{\min} s_* \right) \\ & \stackrel{\eqref{eq:669}}{\ge} \left(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_*+s_*\right) - \alpha^{-1} \left( \left|v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\right|+\frac{s_*}{\hat{\rho}}\right) (\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) \\ & \hspace{5mm} + \left(\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_*+s_*\right) - \alpha^{-1} \left( \left|v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\right|+\frac{s_*}{\hat{\rho}}\right) (\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_*) \\ & = \alpha^{-1} \left(\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_*+s_*\right) \left(\alpha-\left|v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\right|-\frac{s_*}{\hat{\rho}}\right) + \alpha^{-1} \left(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \cdot \mathbf{n}_*+s_*\right) \left(\alpha-\left|v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\right|-\frac{s_*}{\check{\rho}}\right). \end{aligned} \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Split $2(\check{\hat U}\cdot n_*+s_*)$ into two nonnegative-coefficient terms.

nodes.name: Evaluate at the GLF state
nodes.statement: Additionally, for any $\rho_* > 0$ and $z_* > 0$, \begin{align*} & 2 \Big( \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}_* + s_* \Big) = 2 \Big[ \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho (\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{v}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{v}}$} } v-v_{\min}) + h(\rho_*,z_*;\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z) \Big] \\ \stackrel{\rm \Cref{lem:791}}{\ge} & 2 \Big[ \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho (\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{v}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{v}}$} } v-v_{\min}) + h(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z;\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho, \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z) \Big] = 2 \left[\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \cdot \mathbf{n}(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z) + s (\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z) \right] \\ \stackrel{\eqref{eq:726}}{\ge} \hspace{3.5mm} & \alpha^{-1}\left(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}\cdot\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathbf{n}+\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s\right) \left(\alpha-\left|v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\right|-\frac{\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s}{\hat{\rho}}\right) + \alpha^{-1}\left(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}\cdot\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathbf{n}+\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s\right) \left(\alpha-\left|v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\right|-\frac{\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s}{\check{\rho}}\right), \end{align*} where $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\mathbf{n}}}$} } \mathbf{n} := \mathbf{n}(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z)$ and $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s := s(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho,\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z)$.
nodes.statement_short: Use Lemma 2.2 to reduce to the normal at the GLF state.

nodes.name: Reduce to range of GLF density
nodes.statement: Thus, to prove \eqref{eq:656}, we only need to show that $ \alpha \ge \left|v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})\right|+{\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s}/{\hat{\rho}} $ and $ \alpha \ge \left|v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}})\right|+{\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s}/{\check{\rho}} $ . Based on the inequality \eqref{eq:674}, we only need to show $\overline{s}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}},\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \ge \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{s}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{s}}$} } s$. To this end, according to $\overline{s}$ in \eqref{eq:686}, it is sufficient to prove that \begin{equation} \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho \in \big[\,\underline{\rho},\overline{\rho}\,\big], \qquad \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z \in \big[\,\underline{z},\overline{z}\,\big]. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Suffices to show the GLF $\rho$, $z$ lie in $[\underline\rho,\overline\rho]$, $[\underline z,\overline z]$.

nodes.name: Linearity in 1/alpha
nodes.statement: Notice that \begin{align*} \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho = \frac{\hat{\rho}}{2}\left(1+\frac{\hat{v}}{\alpha}\right) +& \frac{\check{\rho}}{2}\left(1-\frac{\check{v}}{\alpha}\right) = \frac{\hat{\rho}+\check{\rho}}{2} + \alpha^{-1} \left( \frac{\hat{\rho}\hat{v}-\check{\rho}\check{v}}{2} \right), \\ \mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z = \frac{\hat{z}}{2}\left(1+\frac{\hat{v}}{\alpha}\right) +& \frac{\check{z}}{2}\left(1-\frac{\check{v}}{\alpha}\right) = \frac{\hat{z}+\check{z}}{2} + \alpha^{-1} \left( \frac{\hat{z}\hat{v}-\check{z}\check{v}}{2} \right) \end{align*} are both linear functions with respect to $\alpha^{-1}$.
nodes.statement_short: GLF $\rho$, $z$ are linear in $\alpha^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Based on the condition \eqref{eq:674}, $\alpha^{-1} \in \big(\,0,\alpha_{\rm std}^{-1}\,\big]$, which implies the value of $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho$ (resp. $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.5 pt}{$\check{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.5 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z$) is between $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ (resp. $z_1$ and $z_2$). Thus, \eqref{eq:1010} is true. The proof is completed.
nodes.statement_short: $\alpha^{-1}\in(0,\alpha_{std}^{-1}]$ puts the values in range.

nodes.name: Membership in Omega_2
nodes.statement: On one hand, Since $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}$, $\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \in \Omega \subseteq \Omega_2 = \Omega_2^*$, \Cref{L2} implies that $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \in \Omega_2^* = \Omega_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.5 gives the GLF state in $\Omega_2$.

nodes.name: Membership in Omega_1
nodes.statement: On the other hand, since $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}$, $\widecheck{\mathbf{U}} \in \Omega \subseteq \Omega_1$, and $\alpha > \alpha_{\max}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}, \widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \ge \max\{ v(\widehat{\mathbf{U}}), v(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \}$, \Cref{L1} implies $\mathcal{S}^+_{\tt LF}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})$, $\mathcal{S}^-_{\tt LF}(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \in \Omega_1$. The convexity of $\Omega_1$ (\Cref{lem:466}) implies $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} = \frac12\mathcal{S}^+_{\tt LF}(\widehat{\mathbf{U}})+\frac12\mathcal{S}^-_{\tt LF}(\widecheck{\mathbf{U}}) \in \Omega_1$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 2.3 plus convexity of $\Omega_1$.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Therefore, it holds that $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{0.6 pt}{$\widecheck{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.6 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U} \in \Omega_1 \cap \Omega_2 = \Omega$, and the proof is completed.
nodes.statement_short: GLF state in $\Omega_1\cap\Omega_2=\Omega$.

nodes.name: (i) Convexity of superlevel set
nodes.statement: (i) For any $\lambda \in [0,1]$ and any $\mathbf{U}_0$, $\mathbf{U}_1 \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon \subseteq \mathcal{R}$, the convexity of $\mathcal{R}$ implies that $\mathbf{U}_\lambda = \lambda \mathbf{U}_1 + (1-\lambda) \mathbf{U}_0 \in \mathcal{R}$. Due to the concavity of function $H$, it holds that $H(\mathbf{U}_\lambda) \ge \lambda H(\mathbf{U}_1) + (1-\lambda) H(\mathbf{U}_0) \ge \varepsilon$. Therefore, $\mathbf{U}_\lambda \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ and $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ is convex.
nodes.statement_short: Concavity of $H$ gives convexity of $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: (ii) Unique intersection
nodes.statement: (ii) For $\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \not \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$, the set $\{\mathcal{U}(\theta;\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) : \theta \in [0,1]\}$ forms a line segment connecting $\overline{\mathbf{U}} \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ and $\widehat{\mathbf{U}} \not \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$. This line segment has to intersect with the boundary of $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$, namely, $\{\mathbf{U}\in\mathcal{R}:H(\mathbf{U}) = \varepsilon\}$ and the convexity of $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ also implies that the intersection happens only once. The claim (ii) is proven.
nodes.statement_short: A segment from inside to outside a convex set crosses its boundary once.

nodes.name: (iii) Scaled states admissible
nodes.statement: (iii) Since $\mathbf{U}_0 = \overline{\mathbf{U}} \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ and $\mathcal{U}(\Theta(\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}},H,\varepsilon);\overline{\mathbf{U}},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}) \in \mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$, the convexity of $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$ immediately implies (iii).
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\mathcal{R}_\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Step 1: positivity scaling of rho and z
nodes.statement: [\textbf{Step 1}:] Enforce the positivity of $\rho$ and $z$ by a local scaling \begin{equation} \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x) = \Big( \theta_1 \hat\rho_j^{n,s}(x) +(1-\theta_1)\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.4 pt}{$\bar{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.4 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho_j^{n,s}, \hat y_j^{n,s}(x), \theta_2 \hat z_j^{n,s}(x) +(1-\theta_2)\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.4 pt}{$\bar{\phantom{z}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.4 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{z}}$} } z_j^{n,s} \Big)^\top, \end{equation} where the local scaling coefficients $\{\theta_r\}_{r = 1}^2$ are defined by \[ \theta_r = \min_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} \Theta\Big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_r,\varepsilon_r\Big), \;\; \varepsilon_r = \min \Big\{ 10^{-12} , H_r(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s}) \Big\},\; r = 1,2. \] Here, the $L$-point Gauss--Lobatto nodes in $I_j$ are denoted by $\{x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell} \}_{\ell = 1}^L$, and the positive parameter $\varepsilon_r$ is introduced to enhance the robustness of above limiter under the influence of round-off errors. Also, please note that the local scaling \eqref{eq:1706} does not change the cell average, that is, $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s} = \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}$.
nodes.statement_short: Scale $\rho$ and $z$ toward the cell average so they are positive at Gauss-Lobatto nodes.

nodes.name: Step 2: scaling for remaining constraints
nodes.statement: [\textbf{Step 2}:]Enforce the remaining constraints by \begin{equation} \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s}(x) = \theta_3 \widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x) + (1-\theta_3) \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}, \end{equation} where the local scaling coefficients $\theta_3$ is defined by \[ \theta_3 = \min_{r = 3,\dots,7} \min_{\ell = 1,\dots,L} \Theta\Big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_r,\varepsilon_r\Big), \; \varepsilon_r = \min \Big\{ 10^{-12} , H_r(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s}) \Big\},\; r = 3,\dots,7. \] The local scaling \eqref{eq:1733} does not change the cell average: $\overline{\mathbf{U}}_{j}^{n,s} = \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s} = \mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}$.
nodes.statement_short: Scale the whole polynomial toward the cell average so $H_3,\dots,H_7\ge\varepsilon$ at Gauss-Lobatto nodes.

nodes.name: Step 1 positivity
nodes.statement: Let us consider an arbitrary $\ell \in \{1,\dots,L\}$. Notice that $H_1(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.4 pt}{$\bar{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.4 pt}{$\hat{\phantom{\rho}}$} } \rho_j^{n,s}) \ge \varepsilon_1$ and $H_1(\cdot)$ is concave in $\mathbb{R}^3$, \Cref{lem:1467} implies $\hat{\rho}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) = H_1\big(\mathcal{U}(\theta_1;\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}))\big) \ge \varepsilon_1$, since $0 \le \theta_1 \le \Theta\big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_j^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_j^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_1,\varepsilon_1\big)$. Similarly, we can prove that $\hat{z}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \ge \varepsilon_2$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.3 for $H_1$, $H_2$.

nodes.name: Intermediate state in Omega_0
nodes.statement: Therefore, $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega_0$ and $\Theta\big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_r,\varepsilon_r\big) = 1$ for $r = 1,2$.
nodes.statement_short: After step 1 the values lie in $\Omega_0$.

nodes.name: Step 2 remaining constraints
nodes.statement: Let us consider an arbitrary $r \in \{1,\dots,7\}$. Since $H_r(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s}) = H_r(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}) \ge \varepsilon_r$, $H_r(\cdot)$ is concave in $\Omega_0$, and $0 \le \theta_3 \le \Theta\big(\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s} (x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}),H_r,\varepsilon_r\big)$ , \Cref{lem:1467} implies $ H_r\big( \mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \big) = H_r\big(\mathcal{U}(\theta_3;\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}_{j,*}^{n,s},\widehat{\mathbf{U}}_{j,*}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}))\big) \ge \varepsilon_r$, that is, $\mathbf{U}_{j}^{n,s}(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega_{j}^{n,s}$.
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.3 for each concave $H_r$ gives membership.

nodes.name: Gauss-Lobatto exactness
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbf{U}_j(x) \in \mathbb{P}^k$, the $L$-point Gauss--Lobatto quadrature holds exactly: \[ \overline{\mathbf{U}}_j = \frac{1}{\Delta x} \int_{I_j} \mathbf{U}_j(x) \, \textrm{d}x = \sum_{\ell = 1}^L \omega^{\tt GL}_\ell \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}). \]
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Cell average equals GL quadrature.

nodes.name: Convex decomposition
nodes.statement: Since $\omega^{\tt GL}_1 = \omega^{\tt GL}_L$, $x^{\tt GL}_{j,1} = x_{j-\frac12}$, $x^{\tt GL}_{j,L} = x_{j+\frac12}$, we can rewrite \eqref{eq:2121} as \begin{equation} \overline{\mathbf{U}}^*_j = \sum_{\ell = 2}^L \omega^{\tt GL}_\ell \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) + (\omega^{\tt GL}_1-\lambda) \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,1}) + (\omega^{\tt GL}_1-\lambda) \mathbf{U}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,L}) + \lambda \mathbf{U}_j^{-} + \lambda \mathbf{U}_j^{+}, \end{equation} where $\lambda := \alpha \frac{\Delta t}{\Delta x} \le \omega^{\tt GL}_1$, and $\mathbf{U}_j^{\pm} := \mathcal{S}_{\tt GLF}(\mathbf{U}^{\pm}_{j-\frac12},\mathbf{U}^{\pm}_{j+\frac12})$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Rewrite FE update as convex combination including GLF states.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 2.6
nodes.statement: \Cref{thm:1471} implies that $\mathbf{U}^{\pm}_j \in \Omega$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: GLF states lie in $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Conclude by convexity
nodes.statement: The convex combination \eqref{eq:2265} implies that $\overline{\mathbf{U}}^*_j \in \Omega$ due to the convexity of $\Omega$ (\Cref{lem:466}). The proof is completed.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Convexity of $\Omega$.

nodes.name: Cell averages in Omega^{n,1}
nodes.statement: Since $\mathbf{U}_j^n \in (\mathbb{P}^k)^3$ for all $j$, the $L$-point Gauss--Lobatto quadrature holds exactly, namely, $ \overline{\mathbf{U}}_j^n = \frac{1}{\Delta x} \int_{I_j} \mathbf{U}^n_j(x) \, \textrm{d} x = \sum_{\ell = 1}^{L} \omega^{\tt GL} \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}), $ which decomposes $\overline{\mathbf{U}}_j^n$ as a convex combination of $\mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^n$, which leads to $\overline{\mathbf{U}}_j^n \in \Omega^{n} = \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1}$ due to the convexity of $\Omega$ (\Cref{lem:466}) and the hierarchy of global invariant domains (\Cref{lem:1889}).
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: GL exactness, convexity and nestedness give $\overline U_j^n\in\Omega^{n,1}$.

nodes.name: Edge values in Omega^{n,1}
nodes.statement: Additionally, all the cell-edge values of $\mathbf{U}^n_h$ belong to $\Omega^{n,1}$, since (i) For $j = 1,\dots,N_x$, $\mathbf{U}^n_h(x_{j-\frac12}^{+}) = \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,1}) \in \Omega^{n} = \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1}$, $\mathbf{U}^n_h(x_{j+\frac12}^{-}) = \mathbf{U}^n_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,L}) \in \Omega^{n} = \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1}$; (ii) By \Cref{lem:1872}, $\mathbf{U}^n_h(x_{\frac12}^{-}) \in \Omega^{n,1}$ and $\mathbf{U}^n_h(x_{N_x+\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,1}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Interior and boundary edge values lie in $\Omega^{n,1}$.

nodes.name: FE step and OE
nodes.statement: Therefore, we can apply \Cref{lem:2154} on $\mathbf{U}^n_h$ to obtain $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widetilde{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}$ for all $j$, and then \Cref{lem:1625b} to obtain $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}$ for all $j$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.5 and Prop. 3.1 for the first stage.

nodes.name: Apply limiter
nodes.statement: After applying the BP limiter to $\widehat{\mathbf{U}}^{n,1}_h$, \Cref{lem:1775} implies that the first RK stage is BP, namely, $\overline{\mathbf{U}}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}, \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_h(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,1}$ for all $j$ and $\ell$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.4: first RK stage is BP.

nodes.name: Later RK stages
nodes.statement: Using similar arguments, we can prove the BP properties of the second and third RK stages: $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_h(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,s}$ for any $j$, $\ell$, and $s = 2,3$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Same argument for stages 2 and 3.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Noticing that $\mathbf{U}^{n+1}_h = \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h$ and $\Omega^{n+1} = \Omega^{n,3}$, the claim \eqref{eq:2177} is proven.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Final stage gives the claim.

nodes.name: Four cases
nodes.statement: Let us consider four cases:
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Split by cell position.

nodes.name: Case (i) interior left edges
nodes.statement: [(i)] If $j = 2,\dots,N_x$, then from \eqref{eq:1851}--\eqref{eq:1982}, we can obtain \begin{equation*} \left. \begin{aligned} && \mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-}) = \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j-1}(x^{\tt GL}_{j-1,L})\\ && \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j-1}(x^{\tt GL}_{j-1,L}) \in \Omega^{n, 0}_{j-1} \subseteq \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1} \\ && \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j-1}(x^{-}_{j-\frac12}) \in \Omega^{n, 0}_{j, *} \end{aligned} \right\} \; \Rightarrow \; \mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-}) \in \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n, 0}_{j, *} = \Omega^{n, 1}_{j}. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Left edge values lie in $\Omega^{n,1}_j$.

nodes.name: Case (ii) j = 1
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Left boundary state lies in $\Omega^{n,1}_1$.

nodes.name: Case (iii) interior right edges
nodes.statement: [(iii)] If $j = 1,\dots,N_x-1$, then from \eqref{eq:1851}--\eqref{eq:1982}, we can obtain \begin{equation*} \left. \begin{aligned} && \mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+}) = \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j+1}(x^{\tt GL}_{j+1,1}) \\ && \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j+1}(x^{\tt GL}_{j+1,1}) \in \Omega^{n, 0}_{j+1} \subseteq \Omega^{n,0} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1} \\ && \mathbf{U}^{n}_{j+1}(x^{+}_{j+\frac12}) \in \Omega^{n, 0}_{j, *} \end{aligned} \right\} \;\Rightarrow \; \mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n, 0}_{j, *} = \Omega^{n, 1}_{j}. \end{equation*}
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Right edge values lie in $\Omega^{n,1}_j$.

nodes.name: Case (iv) j = N_x
nodes.statement: [(iv)] If $j = N_x$, $\mathbf{U}^{n,0}_h(x_{N_x +\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{N_x,*} = \Omega^{n,1}_{N_x}$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Right boundary state lies in $\Omega^{n,1}_{N_x}$.

nodes.name: Summarize edge values
nodes.statement: To summarize, $\mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j-\frac12}^{-}) \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ and $\mathbf{U}_h^{n,0}(x_{j+\frac12}^{+}) \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for $j = 1,\dots,N_x$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: All edge values in $\Omega_j^{n,1}$.

nodes.name: GL values in Omega_j^{n,1}
nodes.statement: On the other hand, \eqref{eq:1851}--\eqref{eq:1927} implies that $\mathbf{U}_h(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,0} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{j,*} \subseteq \Omega^{n,1} \cap \Omega^{n,0}_{j,*} = \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for all $j$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Interior GL values lie in $\Omega^{n,1}_j$.

nodes.name: FE step and OE
nodes.statement: Therefore, we can use \Cref{lem:2154} to obtain $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widetilde{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for all $j$, and then \Cref{lem:1625b} to obtain $\mathrlap{ \raisebox{1.2 pt}{$\overline{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathrlap{ \raisebox{-0.9 pt}{$\widehat{\phantom{\mathbf{U}}}$} } \mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for all $j$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.5 and Prop. 3.1.

nodes.name: Apply limiter
nodes.statement: Following this, we may apply \Cref{lem:1775} to conclude with the local BP property of the first RK stage, namely, $\mathbf{U}^{n,1}_j(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,1}_j$ for all $j$ and $\ell$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Lemma 4.4: first stage locally BP.

nodes.name: Later RK stages
nodes.statement: Via the similar arguments, we can prove the local BP properties of the second and the third RK stages: $\mathbf{U}^{n,s}_h(x^{\tt GL}_{j,\ell}) \in \Omega^{n,s}$ for all $j$, $\ell$, and $s = 2,3$.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Same for stages 2 and 3.

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Noticing $\mathbf{U}^{n+1}_h = \mathbf{U}^{n,3}_h$ and $\Omega^{n+1} = \Omega^{n,3}$, the claim \eqref{eq:2274} is proven.
nodes.section: 4.3 Proving BP property of BP-OEDG schemes
nodes.statement_short: Final stage gives the claim.
